```ts
  test("each has its target type, and a target id in PostgreSQL's lower-case spelling only", () => {
    expect(STAFF_STEP_UP_ACTIONS.case_decided.targetType).toBe("case");
    expect(STAFF_STEP_UP_ACTIONS.appeals_reviewed.targetType).toBe("decision");
    expect(STAFF_STEP_UP_ACTIONS.identity_revealed.targetType).toBe("intake_item");
    for (const action of ["case_decided", "appeals_reviewed", "identity_revealed"] as const) {
      const spec = STAFF_STEP_UP_ACTIONS[action];
      expect(spec.targetId.safeParse(uuid).success, action).toBe(true);
      expect(spec.targetId.safeParse(uuid.toUpperCase()).success, action).toBe(false);
      expect(spec.targetId.safeParse("abc").success, action).toBe(false);
    }
  });

  test("case_decided takes an interim, a final and a correcting decision, each exactly as sent", () => {
    for (const params of [interim, final, noAction, legal, correction]) expect(decided.parse(params), params.kind).toEqual(params);
    everyFieldRequired(decided, interim);
    // A final decision that finds no breach may still name the rule it examined, and may lift the case's interim withholds.
    expect(decided.parse({ ...noAction, ground: "incompatible", ruleId: "R5", actions: [{ kind: "restore", mediaId: null }] }).ruleId).toBe("R5");
    expect(decided.parse({ ...noAction, outcome: "not_evident" }).outcome).toBe("not_evident");
    expect(decided.parse({ ...legal, categoryKeyword: "KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT" }).categoryKeyword).toBe("KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT");
  });

  test("the params are strict and unchanged: a member they do not know is refused, and nothing is trimmed, folded or defaulted", () => {
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, note: "x" })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, actions: [{ kind: "withhold", mediaId: null, extra: 1 }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(reviewed, { ...review, ground: null })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(revealed, { ...reveal, text: "why" })).toBe(true);
    // No transform: an upper-case id or digest is refused, never lower-cased.
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, snapshotId: uuid.toUpperCase() })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, snapshotDigest: hex.toUpperCase() })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, factsDigest: ` ${hex}` })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, actions: [{ kind: "withhold_media", mediaId: image.toUpperCase() }] })).toBe(true);
    // Numbers are whole and in range.
    for (const stateVersion of [-1, 1.5, "0", 2_147_483_648]) expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, stateVersion }), String(stateVersion)).toBe(true);
    for (const rulesVersion of [0, 1.5, 32_768]) expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, rulesVersion }), String(rulesVersion)).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PORNOGRAPHY_OR_SEXUALIZED_CONTENT" })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, ruleId: "R7" })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, kind: "review" })).toBe(true);
  });

  test("the outcome goes with the kind: an interim decision restricts, a final one restricts or finds no breach, a correction reverses", () => {
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, outcome: "no_violation" })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...final, outcome: "kept" })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...final, outcome: "reversed" })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...correction, outcome: "restricted" })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...correction, outcome: "kept" })).toBe(true);
    expect(decided.parse({ ...correction, outcome: "partly_reversed" }).outcome).toBe("partly_reversed");
    expect(refused(reviewed, { ...review, outcome: "restricted" })).toBe(true);
    expect(reviewed.parse({ ...review, outcome: "kept", actions: [] }).outcome).toBe("kept");
  });

  test("an interim decision answers no item: its throughSeq is 0", () => {
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, throughSeq: 1 })).toBe(true);
    expect(decided.parse({ ...final, throughSeq: 1 }).throughSeq).toBe(1);
  });

  test("a restriction carries its ground, its facts and its reason; a rule ground its rule; a legal ground its reference, and no rule", () => {
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, ground: null, ruleId: null })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, factsDigest: null })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, reasonDigest: null })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, ruleId: null })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...legal, legalReferenceDigest: null })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...legal, ruleId: "R3" })).toBe(true);
  });

  test("a keyword goes only with the ground of the law", () => {
    expect(refused(decided, { ...final, categoryKeyword: "KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT" })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...noAction, categoryKeyword: "KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT" })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...legal, categoryKeyword: "KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL" })).toBe(true);
  });

  test("a correction names the decision it corrects, states no ground of its own, and holds reversals only; no other kind names a decision", () => {
    expect(refused(decided, { ...correction, reviewsDecisionId: null })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...correction, reasonDigest: null })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...correction, ground: "incompatible", ruleId: "R1" })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...correction, ruleId: "R1" })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...correction, factsDigest: hex })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...correction, legalReferenceDigest: hex })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...correction, categoryKeyword: "KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT" })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...correction, actions: [{ kind: "withhold", mediaId: null }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...correction, actions: [{ kind: "restore", mediaId: null }, { kind: "seal_media", mediaId: null }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(decided.parse({ ...correction, actions: [{ kind: "unseal_media", mediaId: null }] }).actions).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, reviewsDecisionId: uuid })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...final, reviewsDecisionId: uuid })).toBe(true);
  });

  test("the actions are sorted by kind and then by image, without repeats, at most eight, with at most one post measure and one seal", () => {
    const sorted = [
      { kind: "remove", mediaId: null },
      { kind: "remove_media", mediaId: image },
      { kind: "remove_media", mediaId: otherImage },
      { kind: "seal_media", mediaId: null },
    ];
    const sealing = { ...final, ruleId: "R2", category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS", actions: sorted };
    expect(decided.parse(sealing).actions).toEqual(sorted);
    // Any other order of the same actions, and any repeat, is refused: the same decision always has the same hash.
    expect(refused(decided, { ...sealing, actions: [sorted[1], sorted[0], sorted[2], sorted[3]] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...sealing, actions: [sorted[0], sorted[2], sorted[1], sorted[3]] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...sealing, actions: [sorted[0], sorted[1], sorted[1], sorted[3]] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...sealing, actions: [sorted[0], sorted[3], sorted[3]] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, actions: [{ kind: "withhold", mediaId: null }, { kind: "withhold", mediaId: null }] })).toBe(true);
    // Two post measures in one decision.
    expect(refused(decided, { ...final, actions: [{ kind: "remove", mediaId: null }, { kind: "withhold", mediaId: null }] })).toBe(true);
    // Nine actions.
    const nine = Array.from({ length: 9 }, (_, i) => ({ kind: "remove_media", mediaId: `${i}a1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a` }));
    expect(refused(decided, { ...final, actions: nine })).toBe(true);
    expect(decided.parse({ ...final, actions: nine.slice(0, 8) }).actions).toHaveLength(8);
  });

  test("an image measure names its image, and no other kind names one", () => {
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, actions: [{ kind: "withhold_media", mediaId: null }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, actions: [{ kind: "withhold", mediaId: image }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...final, actions: [{ kind: "seal_media", mediaId: image }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...correction, actions: [{ kind: "restore_media", mediaId: null }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(decided.parse({ ...interim, actions: [{ kind: "withhold_media", mediaId: image }] }).actions[0]).toEqual({ kind: "withhold_media", mediaId: image });
  });

  test("appeals_reviewed takes the appeal, the snapshot, the outcome and reversals only, sorted like a decision's", () => {
    expect(reviewed.parse(review)).toEqual(review);
    everyFieldRequired(reviewed, review);
    expect(refused(reviewed, { ...review, actions: [{ kind: "remove", mediaId: null }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(reviewed, { ...review, actions: [{ kind: "restore_media", mediaId: otherImage }, { kind: "restore_media", mediaId: image }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(reviewed, { ...review, actions: [{ kind: "restore", mediaId: null }, { kind: "restore", mediaId: null }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(reviewed, { ...review, appealId: uuid.toUpperCase() })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(reviewed, { ...review, reasonDigest: null })).toBe(true);
    expect(reviewed.parse({ ...review, outcome: "partly_reversed", actions: [{ kind: "restore_media", mediaId: image }, { kind: "unseal_media", mediaId: null }] }).actions).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3e (design, section 10.4)
  const accountFinal = { ...final, ruleId: "R1" };
  const suspendAction = (days: number | null, announced: boolean) => ({ kind: "suspend", mediaId: null, days, announced });

  test("3e: an action entry is one of two strict shapes, and the three timed kinds sign their days and whether they are announced", () => {
    const announced = { ...accountFinal, actions: [suspendAction(3, true)] };
    expect(decided.parse(announced)).toEqual(announced);
    expect(decided.parse({ ...accountFinal, actions: [{ kind: "terminate", mediaId: null, days: null, announced: false }] }).actions).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(decided.parse({ ...accountFinal, ruleId: "R6", actions: [{ kind: "restrict_reporting", mediaId: null, days: 30, announced: false }] }).actions).toHaveLength(1);
    // A timed kind in the plain shape, and a plain kind in the timed one, are refused.
    expect(refused(decided, { ...accountFinal, actions: [{ kind: "suspend", mediaId: null }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...accountFinal, actions: [{ kind: "remove", mediaId: null, days: 3, announced: true }] })).toBe(true);
    // days is a whole number from 1 to 30, null only on a termination; a restriction of reporting is never announced.
    for (const days of [0, 31, 1.5]) expect(refused(decided, { ...accountFinal, actions: [suspendAction(days, true)] }), String(days)).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...accountFinal, actions: [suspendAction(null, true)] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...accountFinal, actions: [{ kind: "terminate", mediaId: null, days: 3, announced: true }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...accountFinal, ruleId: "R6", actions: [{ kind: "restrict_reporting", mediaId: null, days: 3, announced: true }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...accountFinal, actions: [{ kind: "suspend", mediaId: image, days: 3, announced: true }] })).toBe(true);
    // At most one suspension or termination.
    expect(refused(decided, { ...accountFinal, actions: [suspendAction(3, true), { kind: "terminate", mediaId: null, days: null, announced: true }] })).toBe(true);
  });

  test("3e: the six measures only in a final restriction, a strike only on a korbat rule other than R2, an overruling only with a full reversal", () => {
    expect(decided.parse({ ...final, actions: [{ kind: "remove", mediaId: null }, { kind: "strike", mediaId: null }] }).actions).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...interim, actions: [{ kind: "strike", mediaId: null }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...noAction, actions: [{ kind: "retire_handle", mediaId: null }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...legal, actions: [{ kind: "remove", mediaId: null }, { kind: "strike", mediaId: null }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...final, ruleId: "R2", category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS", actions: [{ kind: "remove", mediaId: null }, { kind: "strike", mediaId: null }] })).toBe(true);
    const overruling = { ...correction, actions: [{ kind: "overrule", mediaId: null }, { kind: "restore", mediaId: null }] };
    expect(decided.parse(overruling).actions).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...overruling, outcome: "partly_reversed" })).toBe(true);
    expect(reviewed.parse({ ...review, actions: overruling.actions }).actions).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(refused(reviewed, { ...review, outcome: "partly_reversed", actions: overruling.actions })).toBe(true);
    // A review and a correction hold the four new reversals, never a new measure.
    expect(refused(reviewed, { ...review, actions: [{ kind: "strike", mediaId: null }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(reviewed.parse({ ...review, actions: [{ kind: "lift_suspension", mediaId: null }] }).actions).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  test("3e: a correction may keep the decision with no action; unfounded only on a final no-breach decision, sorted; replaced only with a lift", () => {
    const kept = { ...correction, outcome: "kept", actions: [] };
    expect(decided.parse(kept).outcome).toBe("kept");
    expect(refused(decided, { ...kept, actions: [{ kind: "restore", mediaId: null }] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...final, outcome: "kept" })).toBe(true);
    const [first, second] = [uuid, "6f1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a"].sort();
    expect(decided.parse({ ...noAction, unfounded: [first, second] }).unfounded).toEqual([first, second]);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...noAction, unfounded: [second, first] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...noAction, unfounded: [first, first] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...noAction, unfounded: [first!.toUpperCase()] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...final, unfounded: [first] })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...noAction, unfounded: Array.from({ length: 101 }, (_, i) => `${String(i).padStart(8, "0")}-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a`) })).toBe(true);
    const withdrawn = { ...correction, actions: [{ kind: "lift_suspension", mediaId: null }], replaced: true };
    expect(decided.parse(withdrawn).replaced).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...correction, replaced: true })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, { ...accountFinal, actions: [suspendAction(3, true)], replaced: true })).toBe(true);
    // Both members are always present: a decision without them is refused.
    const { unfounded: _u, ...withoutMarks } = interim;
    const { replaced: _r, ...withoutReplaced } = interim;
    expect(refused(decided, withoutMarks)).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(decided, withoutReplaced)).toBe(true);
  });

  test("identity_revealed takes a reason category and the digest of the saved reason, never the reason", () => {
    expect(revealed.parse(reveal)).toEqual(reveal);
    everyFieldRequired(revealed, reveal);
    for (const reasonCategory of ["impersonation_claim", "abuse_of_reporting", "legal_requirement", "other"]) expect(revealed.parse({ ...reveal, reasonCategory }).reasonCategory).toBe(reasonCategory);
    expect(refused(revealed, { ...reveal, reasonCategory: "curiosity" })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(revealed, { ...reveal, reasonDigest: "because" })).toBe(true);
  });

  test("the cross-field rules survive the route's extension with the assertion, since its key does not overlap", () => {
    const extended = decided.extend({ stepUp: AuthenticationResponseJSON.optional() });
    expect(extended.parse({ ...interim, stepUp: assertion })).toEqual({ ...interim, stepUp: assertion });
    expect(extended.parse(interim)).toEqual(interim);
    expect(refused(extended, { ...interim, outcome: "no_violation", stepUp: assertion })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(extended, { ...interim, throughSeq: 2, stepUp: assertion })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(extended, { ...interim, other: 1, stepUp: assertion })).toBe(true);
    const extendedReview = reviewed.extend({ stepUp: AuthenticationResponseJSON.optional() });
    expect(refused(extendedReview, { ...review, actions: [{ kind: "remove", mediaId: null }], stepUp: assertion })).toBe(true);
    expect(extendedReview.parse({ ...review, stepUp: assertion }).stepUp).toEqual(assertion);
  });

  test("the options request takes each of the three with its own target and params", () => {
    const requests = [
      { action: "case_decided", target: { type: "case", id: uuid }, params: interim },
      { action: "appeals_reviewed", target: { type: "decision", id: uuid }, params: review },
      { action: "identity_revealed", target: { type: "intake_item", id: uuid }, params: reveal },
    ];
    for (const request of requests) expect(StaffStepUpOptionsRequest.parse(request), request.action).toEqual(request);
    expect(refused(StaffStepUpOptionsRequest, { ...requests[0], target: { type: "decision", id: uuid } })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(StaffStepUpOptionsRequest, { ...requests[0], params: review })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(StaffStepUpOptionsRequest, { ...requests[0], params: { ...interim, outcome: "kept" } })).toBe(true);
    expect(refused(StaffStepUpOptionsRequest, { ...requests[2], params: {} })).toBe(true);
  });

  /**
   * Every string a params schema lets through, by its path: the walk goes through objects, arrays and nullable members.
   * A string is described by its format (a uuid) and the patterns it is held to; enums and literals are closed lists and
   * numbers are not strings, so neither is listed.
   */
  function strings(schema: unknown, path = "$"): { path: string; format: string | undefined; patterns: string[] }[] {
    const def = (schema as { _zod: { def: Record<string, unknown> } })._zod.def;
    switch (def.type) {
      case "object":
        return Object.entries(def.shape as Record<string, unknown>).flatMap(([key, member]) => strings(member, `${path}.${key}`));
      case "array":
        return strings(def.element, `${path}[]`);
      case "nullable":
      case "optional":
        return strings(def.innerType, path);
      // 3e: an action entry is one of two shapes, each walked; a boolean and a null carry no text.
      case "union":
        return (def.options as unknown[]).flatMap((option) => strings(option, path));
      case "string": {
        const checks = ((def.checks as { _zod: { def: { format?: string; pattern?: RegExp } } }[] | undefined) ?? []).map((check) => check._zod.def);
        return [{ path, format: def.format as string | undefined, patterns: checks.filter((check) => check.format === "regex").map((check) => String(check.pattern)) }];
      }
      case "enum":
      case "literal":
      case "number":
      case "boolean":
      case "null":
        return [];
      default:
        // A kind of member this walk does not know could carry free text: it fails the test until it is listed above.
        return [{ path, format: `unknown member type ${String(def.type)}`, patterns: [] }];
    }
  }
  const LOWER_UUID = "/^[0-9a-f-]+$/";
  const HEX_DIGEST = "/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/";
  const free = (schema: unknown) => strings(schema).filter((s) => !((s.format === "uuid" && s.patterns.includes(LOWER_UUID)) || (s.format === undefined && s.patterns.includes(HEX_DIGEST))));

  test("no params schema of any action lets a free string through: every string is a lower-case uuid or a hex digest", () => {
    // 3f (design, section 10.3): the one named exception, an authority's name and its file number in a correction's facts.
    // They are no words about a person, are bound one line of 1 to 200 characters, and are compared with the order's row.
    const named: Record<string, string[]> = { order_corrected: ["$.facts.authority", "$.facts.reference"] };
    for (const [action, spec] of Object.entries(STAFF_STEP_UP_ACTIONS)) {
      expect(free(spec.params).map((s) => s.path), action).toEqual(named[action] ?? []);
      expect(free(spec.targetId), action).toEqual([]);
    }
    // What the walk finds in the decision's params: ids and digests, nothing else.
    expect(strings(decided).map((s) => s.path)).toEqual(["$.reviewsDecisionId", "$.snapshotId", "$.snapshotDigest", "$.actions[].mediaId", "$.factsDigest", "$.reasonDigest", "$.legalReferenceDigest", "$.unfounded[]"]);
    expect(strings(revealed).map((s) => s.path)).toEqual(["$.reasonDigest"]);
  });

  test("the walk catches a free string, a uuid in any case, a transform and a member it cannot read", () => {
    const loose = z.strictObject({
      note: z.string().max(10),
      id: z.uuid(),
      short: z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{8}$/),
      list: z.array(z.strictObject({ label: z.string().nullable() })),
      trimmed: z.string().trim().pipe(z.uuid()),
      ok: z.uuid().regex(/^[0-9a-f-]+$/),
      digest: z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/).nullable(),
    });
    expect(free(loose).map((s) => s.path)).toEqual(["$.note", "$.id", "$.short", "$.list[].label", "$.trimmed"]);
  });
});

describe("the step-up action's hash and binding", () => {
  const BS = String.fromCharCode(92);
  const LF = String.fromCharCode(10);
  const revoke = { action: "staff_session_revoked", target: { type: "staff_session", id: uuid }, params: {} };
  // The 3a action's sorted JSON, and the sha256 values below, were checked with Python's hashlib when they were written.
  const REVOKE_TEXT = `{"action":"staff_session_revoked","params":{},"target":{"id":"${uuid}","type":"staff_session"}}`;
  const REVOKE_HASH = "dad06ce5248ff75b3aa9b1faec9bab38bfa70f6dd2568d231b02e282207385c5";
  const SESSION = "8a3c7f0e-1111-4222-8333-944445555666";
  const BINDING = "9b70fa1ab475e7958d1265150cd04c7953483fe6145f52b12b2fd89d0c598dca";
  const hexOf = (bytes: Uint8Array) => Array.from(bytes, (b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join("");

  test("the action's text is the sorted JSON of its action, target and params: object keys sorted, no whitespace", () => {
    expect(stepUpActionText(revoke)).toBe(REVOKE_TEXT);
    // The order the members were written in changes nothing.
    expect(stepUpActionText({ params: {}, target: { id: uuid, type: "staff_session" }, action: "staff_session_revoked" })).toBe(REVOKE_TEXT);
    // The options request is hashed as it was sent: its schemas change nothing in it.
    expect(stepUpActionText(StaffStepUpOptionsRequest.parse(revoke))).toBe(REVOKE_TEXT);
  });

  test("params are sorted at every depth, arrays keep their order, and strings and numbers are written as JSON.stringify writes them", () => {
    const params = { b: [3, { z: 1, a: null }, "x"], a: `q"${BS}`, c: true, d: 0.5, e: -0, "": -1, B: { y: [], x: {} } };
    expect(stepUpActionText({ action: "case_decided", target: { type: "post", id: "p1" }, params })).toBe(
      `{"action":"case_decided","params":{"":-1,"B":{"x":{},"y":[]},"a":"q${BS}"${BS}${BS}","b":[3,{"a":null,"z":1},"x"],"c":true,"d":0.5,"e":0},"target":{"id":"p1","type":"post"}}`,
    );
  });

  test("keys are sorted by UTF-16 code units, as Array.prototype.sort sorts them in the API, audit-verify and the console alike", () => {
    const eAcute = String.fromCharCode(0xe9);
    const fullwidthA = String.fromCharCode(0xff21);
    // An astral character's first code unit (0xd83d) sorts before 0xff21, though its code point (0x1f600) is higher.
    const grinning = String.fromCodePoint(0x1f600);
    const params = { [fullwidthA]: 1, [grinning]: 2, [eAcute]: 3, z: 4 };
    expect(stepUpActionText({ action: "a", target: { type: "t", id: "i" }, params })).toBe(
      `{"action":"a","params":{"z":4,"${eAcute}":3,"${grinning}":2,"${fullwidthA}":1},"target":{"id":"i","type":"t"}}`,
    );
  });

  test("a value that is not JSON is refused rather than hashed", () => {
    for (const value of [undefined, Number.NaN, Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY, () => 1, BigInt(1), new Date(0), [undefined], Symbol("x")]) {
      expect(() => stepUpActionText({ action: "a", target: { type: "t", id: "i" }, params: { value } }), String(typeof value)).toThrow(TypeError);
    }
  });

  test("the action's hash is the lower-case hex sha256 of the text's UTF-8 bytes", async () => {

    expect(AuditPage.safeParse({ entries: Array(51).fill(entry), nextCursor: null }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(AuditPage.safeParse({ entries: Array(50).fill(entry), nextCursor: 1 }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(AuditPage.safeParse({ entries: [entry] }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(AuditPage.safeParse({ entries: [entry], nextCursor: 0 }).success).toBe(false);

    expect(AuditPageQuery.parse({ cursor: "42" })).toEqual({ cursor: 42 });
    expect(AuditPageQuery.parse({ at: "7", action: "staff_sign_in" })).toEqual({ at: 7, action: "staff_sign_in" });
    expect(AuditPageQuery.parse({ cursor: "999999999999999" }).cursor).toBe(999_999_999_999_999);
    for (const value of ["0", "-1", "1.5", "01", "1e3", "", " 4", "abc", "1000000000000000"]) {
      expect(AuditPageQuery.safeParse({ cursor: value }).success, value).toBe(false);
      expect(AuditPageQuery.safeParse({ at: value }).success, value).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(AuditPageQuery.safeParse({ action: "role_granted" }).success).toBe(false);
    // A cursor reads older rows and at reads from a place: both at once name no page.
    expect(AuditPageQuery.safeParse({ cursor: "4", at: "7" }).success).toBe(false);
  });
});
```

```ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { actionKind } from "../src/schema/moderation";

/**
 * The rule for the new values of action_kind (3e design, section 6, "The rule for the new enum values"; invariant 1).
 * drizzle's migrator runs every pending migration in one transaction, and a value that ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE added
 * cannot be used as an enum literal before that transaction commits (SQLSTATE 55P04) in anything that is parsed when it
 * is created or run: a view, an SQL-language function, a check, a default, an index predicate, a plain statement. Only a
 * PL/pgSQL body is parsed when it is first called, which no migration statement does. So in 3e's migrations a new value
 * appears as a literal only inside a PL/pgSQL function's body, and everywhere else a kind is compared as text
 * (`kind::text = 'strike'`). This test reads 3e's migration files and refuses any other use.
 *
 * The SQL is read statement by statement, its comments dropped, and every run of white space made one space, so the
 * patterns below need no escapes.
 */

const MIGRATIONS = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "../migrations");

/** 3c's twelve kinds come first in the enum; 3e's ten follow them, and 3f's two follow those (read below). */
const OLD_KINDS = 12;
const KINDS_3E = 10;
const NEW_KINDS: readonly string[] = actionKind.enumValues.slice(OLD_KINDS, OLD_KINDS + KINDS_3E);

/** 3e's first migration: 3c ended at 0019_redaction_scope, so 3e's migrations are 0020 and after. */
const FIRST_3E_MIGRATION = 20;

const NEWLINE = String.fromCharCode(10);
const BREAKPOINT = "--> statement-breakpoint";

/** The journal's entries of 3e's migrations, oldest first. */
function migrationsOf3e(): { idx: number; tag: string }[] {
  const journal = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, "meta", "_journal.json"), "utf8")) as { entries: { idx: number; tag: string }[] };
  return journal.entries.filter((entry) => entry.idx >= FIRST_3E_MIGRATION);
}

/** A statement with its line comments dropped: a comment may name a kind in any words it likes. */
function withoutComments(statement: string): string {
  return statement
    .split(NEWLINE)
    .map((line) => {
      const at = line.indexOf("--");
      return at < 0 ? line : line.slice(0, at);
    })
    .join(NEWLINE);
}

/** Every run of white space (a code point up to the space) as one space, trimmed. */
function flat(text: string): string {
  return [...text]
    .map((char) => (char.charCodeAt(0) <= 32 ? " " : char))
    .join("")
    .split(" ")
    .filter((word) => word !== "")
    .join(" ");
}

/**
 * A statement with the body of a PL/pgSQL function blanked, so that only what is parsed at once is left: a statement that
 * creates a function in LANGUAGE plpgsql keeps its signature and loses what lies between its outer dollar quotes. A DO
 * block keeps its body: it runs inside the migration, and its literals are parsed then.
 */
function withoutPlpgsqlBody(statement: string): string {
  const upper = statement.toUpperCase();
  const creates = upper.startsWith("CREATE FUNCTION") || upper.startsWith("CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION");
  if (!creates || !upper.includes("LANGUAGE PLPGSQL")) return statement;
  const open = statement.indexOf("$$");
  const close = statement.lastIndexOf("$$");
  if (open < 0 || close <= open) return statement;
  return `${statement.slice(0, open + 2)} ${statement.slice(close)}`;
}

/**
 * The places where a literal is compared as text: `::text` followed by `=`, `<>`, `IN (` or `= ANY (ARRAY[` and then a
 * list of quoted words. A new kind's literal there is a text, and parses whatever the enum holds.
 */
const TEXT_COMPARISON = /::text ?(?:=|<>|!=|in ?[(]|= ?any ?[(] ?array ?[[]) ?'[a-z_]+'(?: ?, ?'[a-z_]+')*/gi;

/** The statement that adds a value names it, as a label and not as a literal of the enum. */
const ADDED_VALUE = /alter type [^ ]+ add value '[a-z_]+'/gi;

/** Every use of a new kind's literal in the SQL that is outside a PL/pgSQL body and not compared as text, each with its context. */
function enumLiteralViolations(sqlText: string, kinds: readonly string[] = NEW_KINDS): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  const literal = new RegExp(`'(${kinds.join("|")})'`, "g");
  for (const statement of sqlText.split(BREAKPOINT)) {
    const scanned = withoutPlpgsqlBody(flat(withoutComments(statement)));
    const allowed: [number, number][] = [];
    for (const pattern of [TEXT_COMPARISON, ADDED_VALUE]) {
      for (const match of scanned.matchAll(pattern)) allowed.push([match.index, match.index + match[0].length]);
    }
    for (const match of scanned.matchAll(literal)) {
      const at = match.index;
      const castToText = /^ ?::text(?![a-z_])/i.test(scanned.slice(at + match[0].length));
      if (castToText || allowed.some(([from, to]) => at >= from && at < to)) continue;
      violations.push(scanned.slice(Math.max(0, at - 60), at + match[0].length + 20));
    }
  }
  return violations;
}

describe("the enum-literal rule of 3e's migrations", () => {
  test("action_kind's new values are the ten of 3e, after 3c's twelve", () => {
    expect(NEW_KINDS).toEqual(["strike", "suspend", "terminate", "retire_handle", "warn_reporting", "restrict_reporting", "overrule", "lift_suspension", "unretire_handle", "lift_reporting"]);
  });

  test("3e's migrations are there: the schema (0020) and standing_ledger (0021) at least", () => {
    const tags = migrationsOf3e().map((entry) => entry.tag);
    expect(tags.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
    expect(tags[1]).toBe("0021_standing_ledger");
  });

  test("no file of 3e names a new kind as a literal outside a PL/pgSQL body", () => {
    for (const entry of migrationsOf3e()) {
      const text = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, `${entry.tag}.sql`), "utf8");
      expect(enumLiteralViolations(text), entry.tag).toEqual([]);
    }
  });

  test("the files of 3e do name the new kinds, inside PL/pgSQL bodies, so the test reads what it should", () => {
    const ledger = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, `${migrationsOf3e()[1]!.tag}.sql`), "utf8");
    // The same file read without blanking the bodies would hold many: the bodies are where the kinds are used.
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(ledger.split("LANGUAGE plpgsql").join("LANGUAGE sql")).length).toBeGreaterThan(20);
  });

  test("a deliberate violation of each kind is caught, and the allowed forms are not", () => {
    // Caught: a view, an SQL function, a check and an index predicate that name a new kind as the enum, and a cast.
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'strike';`)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS boolean LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind IN ('suspend', 'terminate')) $$;`)).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`ALTER TABLE decision_actions ADD CONSTRAINT c CHECK (kind <> 'overrule');`)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE INDEX i ON decision_actions (created_at) WHERE kind = 'strike';`)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`SELECT 'lift_reporting'::public.action_kind;`)).toHaveLength(1);
    // A DO block runs inside the migration: its body is no exemption.
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`DO $$ BEGIN PERFORM 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'strike'; END $$;`)).toHaveLength(1);
    // Two statements: the second's violation is found although the first is a PL/pgSQL function.
    const two = `CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN PERFORM 1; END $$;${BREAKPOINT}${NEWLINE}CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'suspend';`;
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(two)).toHaveLength(1);
    // Allowed: a comparison as text, a cast to text, any literal inside a PL/pgSQL body, an old kind, a comment, and the
    // statement that adds the value.
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind::text = 'strike' AND a.kind::text IN ('suspend', 'terminate');`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 'strike'::text AS k;`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN PERFORM 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'strike'; END $$;`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'remove';`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`-- a.kind = 'strike' in a comment${NEWLINE}SELECT 1;`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`ALTER TYPE "public"."action_kind" ADD VALUE 'strike';`)).toEqual([]);
  });
});

/**
 * 3f (design, section 6, "The rule for the new enum values"; invariant 1): the migration orders adds eight values to seven
 * enums: action_kind's disable_by_order and reinstate_by_order, `order` to decision_kind, decision_source and intake_kind,
 * `authority` to intake_channel and `disabled` to moderation_level and post_state. drizzle runs 3f's migrations in one
 * transaction with any others pending, so the rule binds the file that adds them and every later one. The file before it
 * (0026_messages_alerts) names `order` only as a value of a text column, before any enum holds it, so it is not read.
 */
const VALUES_3F: readonly string[] = ["disable_by_order", "reinstate_by_order", "order", "authority", "disabled"];

/** The journal's entries from the migration that adds 3f's values, oldest first. */
function migrationsFromOrders(): { idx: number; tag: string }[] {
  const journal = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, "meta", "_journal.json"), "utf8")) as { entries: { idx: number; tag: string }[] };
  const first = journal.entries.find((entry) => entry.tag.endsWith("_orders"));
  return first === undefined ? [] : journal.entries.filter((entry) => entry.idx >= first.idx);
}

describe("the enum-literal rule of 3f's migrations", () => {
  test("the migration orders is there, and it adds the eight values", () => {
    const files = migrationsFromOrders();
    expect(files[0]?.tag).toBe("0027_orders");
    const text = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, `${files[0]!.tag}.sql`), "utf8");
    const added = [...flat(text).matchAll(/ALTER TYPE "public"."([a-z_]+)" ADD VALUE '([a-z_]+)'/g)].map((m) => `${m[1]}.${m[2]}`).sort();
    expect(added).toEqual(
      [

        "action_kind.reinstate_by_order",
        "decision_kind.order",
        "decision_source.order",

        "intake_kind.order",
        "moderation_level.disabled",
        "post_state.disabled",

  test("no file from the migration orders on names a new value as a literal outside a PL/pgSQL body", () => {

      expect(enumLiteralViolations(text, VALUES_3F), entry.tag).toEqual([]);
    }
  });

  test("a deliberate violation of 3f's values is caught, and the allowed forms are not", () => {
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`ALTER TABLE decisions ADD CONSTRAINT c CHECK (kind <> 'order');`, VALUES_3F)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM posts p WHERE p.moderation_level = 'disabled';`, VALUES_3F)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS boolean LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM intakes i WHERE i.channel = 'authority') $$;`, VALUES_3F)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`ALTER TABLE decisions ADD CONSTRAINT c CHECK (outcome <> 'restricted' OR kind::text = 'order');`, VALUES_3F)).toEqual([]);
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";

const byName = new Map(tables.map((t) => [getTableConfig(t).name, getTableConfig(t)]));

  test("auth tables live in the auth schema", () => {
    for (const name of ["users", "devices", "sessions", "email_codes", "passkeys", "auth_events"]) {
      expect(byName.get(name)?.schema, name).toBe("auth");
    }
  });

  });
});

describe("row level security", () => {
  test("every table has RLS enabled and at least one policy", () => {
    expect(tables.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (const t of tables) {
      const cfg = getTableConfig(t);
      expect(cfg.enableRLS, cfg.name).toBe(true);
      expect(cfg.policies.length, cfg.name).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  });
});

    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "state")?.notNull).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.checks.map((c) => c.name)).toContain("posts_body_len");
  });
  test("join tables have composite primary keys", () => {
    for (const name of ["follows", "likes", "reposts", "bookmarks", "blocks", "mutes"]) {
      expect(byName.get(name)!.primaryKeys.length, name).toBe(1);
      expect(byName.get(name)!.primaryKeys[0]!.columns.length, name).toBe(2);
    }
  });
});

describe("trust and safety schema", () => {

    // 28 before 3c, minus the five retired tables, plus the twelve moderation tables and the four auth tables; then 3e's
    // three: suspension_replies, unfounded_marks and report_tallies; then 3f's first four: contact_messages, alert_outbox,
    // notify_state and notify_folders; then the three of order records: legal_orders, legal_order_items and

  });
  test("auth_events policies allow only insert and select", () => {
    expect(byName.get("auth_events")?.policies.map((p) => p.for).sort()).toEqual(["insert", "select"]);
  });
  test("email code purposes include reauth", () => {
    expect(schema.emailCodePurpose.enumValues).toContain("reauth");
  });
});

describe("posting and feed 2a", () => {

    const posts = byName.get("posts")!;
    const postCols = posts.columns.map((c) => c.name);
    expect(postCols).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(["like_count", "repost_count", "reply_count", "quote_count", "deleted_at"]));
    for (const name of ["like_count", "repost_count", "reply_count", "quote_count"]) {
      expect(posts.columns.find((c) => c.name === name)?.notNull, name).toBe(true);

    expect(posts.checks.map((c) => c.name)).toContain("posts_counts_nonnegative");
    const profiles = byName.get("profiles")!;

    expect(profiles.checks.map((c) => c.name)).toContain("profiles_counts_nonnegative");
  });

    expect(byName.get("posts")!.indexes.map((i) => i.config.name)).toContain("posts_quote_of_idx");
  });
});

describe("images 2b", () => {

    const cols = byName.get("post_media")!.columns;
    expect(cols.map((c) => c.name)).not.toContain("path");
    for (const name of ["post_id", "position", "width", "height", "blurhash"]) {

describe("account lifecycle 1b", () => {
  test("handle_history reserves every lowercase handle a profile ever had, and goes with the profile", () => {
    const cfg = byName.get("handle_history")!;
    expect(cfg.schema).toBeUndefined(); // public
    // retired_at (3e design, section 6.1): set only by a retirement in the ledger, forced null at insert.
    expect(cfg.columns.map((c) => c.name)).toEqual(["handle_lower", "profile_id", "changed_at", "retired_at"]);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "retired_at")?.notNull).toBe(false);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "retired_at")?.hasDefault).toBe(false);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "handle_lower")?.primary).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "profile_id")?.notNull).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "changed_at")?.notNull).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "changed_at")?.hasDefault).toBe(true);
    const fk = cfg.foreignKeys.map((k) => ({ table: getTableConfig(k.reference().foreignTable).name, columns: k.reference().foreignColumns.map((c) => c.name), onDelete: k.onDelete }));
    expect(fk).toEqual([{ table: "profiles", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "cascade" }]);
    expect(cfg.policies.map((p) => [p.name, p.for])).toEqual([["handle_history_api_all", "all"]]);
  });
  test("profiles record when the handle last changed; users record when their purge finished", () => {
    const handleChangedAt = byName.get("profiles")!.columns.find((c) => c.name === "handle_changed_at");
    expect(handleChangedAt).toBeDefined();
    expect(handleChangedAt?.notNull).toBe(false);
    const purgedAt = byName.get("users")!.columns.find((c) => c.name === "purged_at");
    expect(purgedAt).toBeDefined();
    expect(purgedAt?.notNull).toBe(false);
  });
  test("one phone per account: a unique index on phone_hash that leaves out the accounts without one", () => {
    const idx = byName.get("users")!.indexes.find((i) => i.config.name === "users_phone_hash_idx");
    expect(idx?.config.unique).toBe(true);
    expect(idx?.config.columns.map((c) => (c as { name?: string }).name)).toEqual(["phone_hash"]);
    expect(idx?.config.where).toBeDefined();
  });
  test("email codes can be for deleting the account, and every account event of 1b has a type", () => {
    expect(schema.emailCodePurpose.enumValues).toContain("delete_account");
    const values = schema.authEventType.enumValues;
    expect(values.slice(values.indexOf("not_me"), values.indexOf("account_deleted") + 1)).toEqual([
      "not_me",
      "profile_updated",
      "handle_changed",
      "email_changed",
      "badge_verified",
      "badge_removed",
      "export_created",
      "account_deleted",
    ]);
  });
});

describe("passkeys 1c", () => {
  const column = (table: string, name: string) => byName.get(table)!.columns.find((c) => c.name === name);
  /** The foreign keys of one local column: the table and columns they point at and what a delete there does. */
  const foreignKeys = (table: string, name: string) =>
    byName
      .get(table)!
      .foreignKeys.filter((k) => k.reference().columns.some((c) => c.name === name))
      .map((k) => ({ table: getTableConfig(k.reference().foreignTable).name, columns: k.reference().foreignColumns.map((c) => c.name), onDelete: k.onDelete }));

  test("bytea is the bytea SQL type and hands Buffers both ways", () => {
    const table = pgTable("bytea_probe", { value: bytea("value") });
    const probe = getTableConfig(table).columns[0]!;
    expect(probe.getSQLType()).toBe("bytea");
    const bytes = Buffer.from([0, 1, 254, 255]);
    expect(probe.mapToDriverValue(bytes)).toEqual(bytes);
    // postgres.js already parses bytea into a Buffer; a driver that answers a plain Uint8Array gets one too.
    const read = probe.mapFromDriverValue(new Uint8Array([0, 1, 254, 255]));
    expect(Buffer.isBuffer(read)).toBe(true);
    expect(read).toEqual(bytes);
    expect(probe.mapFromDriverValue(bytes)).toEqual(bytes);
  });

  test("users carry an optional WebAuthn user handle in bytea, unique among the accounts that have one", () => {
    const handle = column("users", "webauthn_user_id");
    expect(handle?.getSQLType()).toBe("bytea");
    expect(handle?.notNull).toBe(false);
    expect(handle?.hasDefault).toBe(false);
    const idx = byName.get("users")!.indexes.find((i) => i.config.name === "users_webauthn_user_id_idx");
    expect(idx?.config.unique).toBe(true);
    expect(idx?.config.columns.map((c) => (c as { name?: string }).name)).toEqual(["webauthn_user_id"]);
    expect(idx?.config.where).toBeDefined();
  });

  test("passkeys record the AAGUID, the backup and verification flags, the creating device and a suspected copy", () => {
    expect(column("passkeys", "aaguid")?.getSQLType()).toBe("uuid");
    expect(column("passkeys", "aaguid")?.notNull).toBe(false);
    for (const name of ["backup_eligible", "uv_initialized"]) {
      expect(column("passkeys", name)?.getSQLType(), name).toBe("boolean");
      expect(column("passkeys", name)?.notNull, name).toBe(true);
      expect(column("passkeys", name)?.default, name).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(column("passkeys", "created_device_id")?.getSQLType()).toBe("uuid");
    expect(column("passkeys", "created_device_id")?.notNull).toBe(false);
    expect(foreignKeys("passkeys", "created_device_id")).toEqual([{ table: "devices", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "set null" }]);
    expect(column("passkeys", "suspect_at")?.getSQLType()).toBe("timestamp with time zone");
    expect(column("passkeys", "suspect_at")?.notNull).toBe(false);
    // One row per credential: the index the foundation created stays.
    const idx = byName.get("passkeys")!.indexes.find((i) => i.config.name === "passkeys_credential_idx");
    expect(idx?.config.unique).toBe(true);
    expect(idx?.config.columns.map((c) => (c as { name?: string }).name)).toEqual(["credential_id"]);
  });

  test("sessions carry a random handle that is unique, the factors they proved and the passkey that started them", () => {
    const handle = column("sessions", "handle");
    expect(handle?.getSQLType()).toBe("uuid");
    expect(handle?.notNull).toBe(true);
    expect(handle?.hasDefault).toBe(true);
    const idx = byName.get("sessions")!.indexes.find((i) => i.config.name === "sessions_handle_idx");
    expect(idx?.config.unique).toBe(true);
    expect(idx?.config.columns.map((c) => (c as { name?: string }).name)).toEqual(["handle"]);
    const factors = column("sessions", "factors");
    expect(factors?.getSQLType()).toBe("jsonb");
    expect(factors?.notNull).toBe(true);
    expect(factors?.hasDefault).toBe(true);
    expect(column("sessions", "passkey_id")?.notNull).toBe(false);
    expect(foreignKeys("sessions", "passkey_id")).toEqual([{ table: "passkeys", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "set null" }]);
  });

  test("adding, removing and a counter regression of a passkey are security events", () => {
    const values = schema.authEventType.enumValues;
    // The slice ends at 1c's last value: 3a appends the staff events after it.
    expect(values.slice(values.indexOf("account_deleted"), values.indexOf("passkey_counter_regression") + 1)).toEqual([
      "account_deleted",
      "passkey_added",
      "passkey_removed",
      "passkey_counter_regression",
    ]);
  });
});

describe("explore 2c", () => {
  const column = (table: string, name: string) => byName.get(table)!.columns.find((c) => c.name === name);
  /** Name, SQL type and not-null of every column, in order. */
  const shape = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.columns.map((c) => [c.name, c.getSQLType(), c.notNull]);
  /** Every foreign key of a table by its local column: the table and columns it points at and what a delete there does. */
  const foreignKeys = (table: string) =>
    Object.fromEntries(
      byName.get(table)!.foreignKeys.map((k) => {
        const ref = k.reference();
        return [ref.columns.map((c) => c.name).join(","), { table: getTableConfig(ref.foreignTable).name, columns: ref.foreignColumns.map((c) => c.name), onDelete: k.onDelete }];
      }),
    );
  const indexColumns = (config: { columns: unknown[] }) => config.columns.map((c) => (c as { name?: string }).name);

  test("profiles carry the author's Explore switch, on by default", () => {
    const flag = column("profiles", "show_in_explore");
    expect(flag?.getSQLType()).toBe("boolean");
    expect(flag?.notNull).toBe(true);
    expect(flag?.default).toBe(true);
  });

  test("explore_runs numbers each ranking with an identity and records its time, formula, counts and duration", () => {
    const cfg = byName.get("explore_runs")!;
    expect(cfg.schema).toBeUndefined(); // public
    expect(shape("explore_runs")).toEqual([
      ["generation", "integer", true],
      ["as_of", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      ["formula", "smallint", true],
      ["candidates", "integer", true],
      ["items", "integer", true],
      ["took_ms", "integer", true],
    ]);
    const generation = column("explore_runs", "generation");
    expect(generation?.primary).toBe(true);
    // Always generated: an insert cannot choose its generation, so the numbers come from the sequence alone.
    expect(generation?.generatedIdentity?.type).toBe("always");
    // The refresh writes every other value itself, the refresh time included, which tests move.
    expect(cfg.columns.filter((c) => c.hasDefault).map((c) => c.name)).toEqual(["generation"]);
    expect(cfg.foreignKeys).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("explore_items holds a ranking's posts by position, each post once, and goes with its ranking, its post or its author", () => {
    const cfg = byName.get("explore_items")!;
    expect(cfg.schema).toBeUndefined(); // public
    // No score or count is stored: the position is the order.
    expect(shape("explore_items")).toEqual([
      ["generation", "integer", true],
      ["position", "integer", true],
      ["post_id", "uuid", true],
      ["author_id", "uuid", true],
    ]);
    expect(cfg.primaryKeys.map((k) => k.columns.map((c) => c.name))).toEqual([["generation", "position"]]);
    expect(cfg.indexes.map((i) => [i.config.name, indexColumns(i.config), i.config.unique])).toEqual([["explore_items_generation_post_idx", ["generation", "post_id"], true]]);
    expect(foreignKeys("explore_items")).toEqual({
      generation: { table: "explore_runs", columns: ["generation"], onDelete: "cascade" },
      post_id: { table: "posts", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "cascade" },
      author_id: { table: "profiles", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "cascade" },
    });
  });

  test("both tables have row level security and one full-access policy for the API role", () => {
    // The loop under "row level security" covers them too; this pins the policy each one has.
    for (const name of ["explore_runs", "explore_items"]) {
      const cfg = byName.get(name)!;
      expect(cfg.enableRLS, name).toBe(true);
      expect(cfg.policies.map((p) => [p.name, p.for, p.to]), name).toEqual([[`${name}_api_all`, "all", apiRole]]);
    }
  });

  test("likes and reposts have a BRIN index on created_at for the refresh's window; bookmarks, which Explore never reads, has none", () => {
    for (const name of ["likes", "reposts"]) {
      const brin = byName.get(name)!.indexes.filter((i) => i.config.method === "brin");
      expect(brin.map((i) => [i.config.name, indexColumns(i.config), i.config.unique, i.config.where]), name).toEqual([[`${name}_created_brin`, ["created_at"], false, undefined]]);
    }
    expect(byName.get("bookmarks")!.indexes.filter((i) => i.config.method === "brin")).toEqual([]);
    // The factory's other indexes stay the same on all three tables.
    for (const name of ["likes", "reposts", "bookmarks"]) {
      const others = byName.get(name)!.indexes.filter((i) => i.config.method !== "brin");
      expect(others.map((i) => [i.config.name, i.config.method]).sort(), name).toEqual([
        [`${name}_post_idx`, "btree"],
        [`${name}_user_created_idx`, "btree"],
      ]);
    }
  });
});

describe("staff console 3a", () => {
  const column = (table: string, name: string) => byName.get(table)!.columns.find((c) => c.name === name);
  /** Name, SQL type and not-null of every column, in order. */
  const shape = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.columns.map((c) => [c.name, c.getSQLType(), c.notNull]);
  /** Every foreign key of a table by its local columns: the table and columns it points at and what a delete there does. */
  const foreignKeys = (table: string) =>
    Object.fromEntries(
      byName.get(table)!.foreignKeys.map((k) => {
        const ref = k.reference();
        return [ref.columns.map((c) => c.name).join(","), { table: getTableConfig(ref.foreignTable).name, columns: ref.foreignColumns.map((c) => c.name), onDelete: k.onDelete }];
      }),
    );
  /** Every index as its name, its columns and whether it is unique, by name. */
  const indexes = (table: string) =>
    byName
      .get(table)!
      .indexes.map((i) => [i.config.name, i.config.columns.map((c) => (c as { name?: string }).name), i.config.unique])
      .sort((a, b) => String(a[0]).localeCompare(String(b[0])));
  const uniques = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.uniqueConstraints.map((u) => [u.getName(), u.columns.map((c) => c.name)]);
  const checks = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.checks.map((c) => c.name).sort();
  const policies = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.policies.map((p) => [p.name, p.for, p.to]);

  test("the seven staff events close the auth event type, after 1c's passkey events", () => {
    const values = schema.authEventType.enumValues;
    expect(values.slice(values.indexOf("passkey_counter_regression") + 1)).toEqual([
      "staff_enrollment_issued",
      "staff_key_added",
      "staff_key_revoked",
      "staff_key_counter_regression",
      "staff_sign_in",
      "staff_signed_out",
      "staff_session_revoked",
    ]);
  });

  test("the three staff tables live in the auth schema, with row level security and one policy for the auth role", () => {
    for (const name of ["staff_keys", "staff_enrollments", "staff_sessions"]) {
      const cfg = byName.get(name)!;
      expect(cfg.schema, name).toBe("auth");
      expect(cfg.enableRLS, name).toBe(true);
      expect(policies(name), name).toEqual([[`${name}_auth_all`, "all", authRole]]);
    }
  });

  test("a staff key records its credential, its origin and relying party ID, its dates and whether it was revoked or suspect", () => {
    expect(shape("staff_keys")).toEqual([
      ["id", "uuid", true],
      ["user_id", "uuid", true],
      ["credential_id", "text", true],
      ["public_key", "text", true],
      ["counter", "bigint", true],
      ["transports", "text[]", true],
      ["name", "text", true],
      ["aaguid", "uuid", false],
      ["origin", "text", true],
      ["rp_id", "text", true],
      ["created_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      ["last_used_at", "timestamp with time zone", false],
      ["revoked_at", "timestamp with time zone", false],
      ["suspect_at", "timestamp with time zone", false],
    ]);
    // No user handle of its own: staff registrations use the account's webauthn_user_id.
    expect(column("staff_keys", "user_handle")).toBeUndefined();
    // The development cleaner deletes accounts as the superuser; a key must stop that delete, never go with it.
    expect(foreignKeys("staff_keys")).toEqual({ user_id: { table: "users", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "restrict" } });
    expect(indexes("staff_keys")).toEqual([
      ["staff_keys_credential_idx", ["credential_id"], true],
      ["staff_keys_user_idx", ["user_id"], false],
    ]);
    // The pair the staff sessions' foreign key names.
    expect(uniques("staff_keys")).toEqual([["staff_keys_id_user_id_unique", ["id", "user_id"]]]);
    expect(checks("staff_keys")).toEqual(["staff_keys_suspect_is_revoked"]);
  });

  test("an enrolment keeps only its token's hash, the console it was issued for, its expiry and when it was used", () => {
    expect(shape("staff_enrollments")).toEqual([
      ["id", "uuid", true],
      ["user_id", "uuid", true],
      ["token_hash", "text", true],
      ["origin", "text", true],
      ["rp_id", "text", true],
      ["created_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      ["expires_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      ["used_at", "timestamp with time zone", false],
    ]);
    expect(foreignKeys("staff_enrollments")).toEqual({ user_id: { table: "users", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "cascade" } });
    expect(indexes("staff_enrollments")).toEqual([
      ["staff_enrollments_token_hash_idx", ["token_hash"], true],
      ["staff_enrollments_user_idx", ["user_id"], false],
    ]);
  });

  test("a staff session keeps its token's hash, a unique handle, its key and account together, both expiries and the browser label", () => {
    expect(shape("staff_sessions")).toEqual([
      ["id", "text", true],
      ["handle", "uuid", true],
      ["user_id", "uuid", true],
      ["key_id", "uuid", true],
      ["created_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      ["last_used_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      ["idle_expires_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      ["absolute_expires_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      ["revoked_at", "timestamp with time zone", false],
      ["browser", "text", true],
    ]);
    expect(column("staff_sessions", "id")?.primary).toBe(true);
    expect(column("staff_sessions", "handle")?.hasDefault).toBe(true);
    // The key's foreign key names the account as well, so a session's key always belongs to its account.
    expect(foreignKeys("staff_sessions")).toEqual({
      user_id: { table: "users", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "cascade" },
      "key_id,user_id": { table: "staff_keys", columns: ["id", "user_id"], onDelete: "cascade" },
    });
    expect(indexes("staff_sessions")).toEqual([
      ["staff_sessions_handle_idx", ["handle"], true],
      ["staff_sessions_user_idx", ["user_id"], false],
    ]);
    expect(checks("staff_sessions")).toEqual(["staff_sessions_lifetime"]);
  });

  test("audit_log gains the staff session's handle, the key, the action's hash and the step-up, all optional", () => {
    const added = [
      ["staff_session", "uuid"],
      ["key_id", "uuid"],
      ["action_hash", "text"],
      ["step_up", "jsonb"],
    ] as const;
    for (const [name, type] of added) {
      expect(column("audit_log", name)?.getSQLType(), name).toBe(type);
      expect(column("audit_log", name)?.notNull, name).toBe(false);
      expect(column("audit_log", name)?.hasDefault, name).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(checks("audit_log")).toEqual(["audit_log_step_up_complete"]);
  });

  test("audit_log's chain columns are not null, with placeholder defaults that the trigger always overwrites", () => {
    const chain = [
      ["chain_version", "smallint", 0],
      ["chain_seq", "bigint", 0],
      ["prev_hash", "text", ""],
      ["hash", "text", ""],
    ] as const;
    for (const [name, type, placeholder] of chain) {
      expect(column("audit_log", name)?.getSQLType(), name).toBe(type);
      expect(column("audit_log", name)?.notNull, name).toBe(true);
      expect(column("audit_log", name)?.default, name).toBe(placeholder);
    }
    // One index serves the viewer and audit-verify; there is none on (created_at, id).
    expect(indexes("audit_log")).toEqual([["audit_log_chain_seq_idx", ["chain_seq"], true]]);
  });

  test("audit_head holds one row, the newest place and hash, which the API role may only read", () => {
    const cfg = byName.get("audit_head")!;
    expect(cfg.schema).toBeUndefined(); // public
    expect(shape("audit_head")).toEqual([
      ["id", "smallint", true],
      ["seq", "bigint", true],
      ["hash", "text", true],
    ]);
    expect(column("audit_head", "id")?.primary).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.columns.filter((c) => c.hasDefault)).toEqual([]);
    expect(checks("audit_head")).toEqual(["audit_head_single_row"]);
    expect(cfg.enableRLS).toBe(true);
    expect(policies("audit_head")).toEqual([["audit_head_api_select", "select", apiRole]]);
  });
});

describe("moderation cases 3c", () => {
  const column = (table: string, name: string) => byName.get(table)!.columns.find((c) => c.name === name);
  /** Name, SQL type and not-null of every column, in order. */
  const shape = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.columns.map((c) => [c.name, c.getSQLType(), c.notNull]);
  const checks = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.checks.map((c) => c.name).sort();
  const policies = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.policies.map((p) => [p.name, p.for, p.to]);
  const index = (table: string, name: string) => byName.get(table)!.indexes.find((i) => i.config.name === name)?.config;
  const indexColumns = (config: { columns: unknown[] } | undefined) => config?.columns.map((c) => (c as { name?: string }).name);
  /** An index's predicate as the SQL the migration holds. */
  const predicate = (config: { where?: SQL } | undefined) => (config?.where ? new PgDialect().sqlToQuery(config.where).sql : undefined);
  /** Every foreign key of a table by its local columns: the table and columns it points at and what a delete there does. */
  const foreignKeys = (table: string) =>
    Object.fromEntries(
      byName.get(table)!.foreignKeys.map((k) => {
        const ref = k.reference();
        return [ref.columns.map((c) => c.name).join(","), { table: getTableConfig(ref.foreignTable).name, columns: ref.foreignColumns.map((c) => c.name), onDelete: k.onDelete }];
      }),
    );
  /** The columns declared unique by themselves, each with the name of its constraint. */
  const uniques = (table: string) =>
    byName
      .get(table)!
      .columns.filter((c) => c.isUnique)
      .map((c) => [c.uniqueName, [c.name]])
      .sort();

  /** A check's expression as the migration holds it. */
  const checkSql = (table: string, name: string) => new PgDialect().sqlToQuery(byName.get(table)!.checks.find((c) => c.name === name)!.value).sql;

  const MODERATION_TABLES = ["cases", "intakes", "intake_items", "decisions", "decision_actions", "seal_posts", "appeals", "staff_texts", "evidence_snapshots", "case_access_log", "moderation_limits", "media_holds"];
  const AUTH_TABLES = ["notifier_contacts", "notifier_confirmations", "notifier_suppressions", "staff_personal_accounts"];

  test("the twelve moderation tables are public, with row level security and one policy for the API role", () => {
    for (const name of MODERATION_TABLES) {
      const cfg = byName.get(name);
      expect(cfg, name).toBeDefined();
      expect(cfg!.schema, name).toBeUndefined(); // public
      expect(cfg!.enableRLS, name).toBe(true);
      // The grants do the restricting (migration 0015); moderation_limits is read only, so its one policy is a SELECT one.
      expect(policies(name), name).toEqual(name === "moderation_limits" ? [["moderation_limits_api_select", "select", apiRole]] : [[`${name}_api_all`, "all", apiRole]]);
    }
  });

  test("no moderation table has a column named like an email or an address", () => {
    for (const name of MODERATION_TABLES) {
      for (const c of byName.get(name)!.columns) expect(c.name, `${name}.${c.name}`).not.toMatch(/email|address/i);
    }
  });

  test("xid8 is the xid8 SQL type and hands the transaction id over as a string", () => {
    const table = pgTable("xid8_probe", { value: xid8("value") });
    const probe = getTableConfig(table).columns[0]!;
    expect(probe.getSQLType()).toBe("xid8");
    // A 64-bit counter: a string keeps every digit, where a JavaScript number would not.
    expect(probe.mapFromDriverValue("18446744073709551615")).toBe("18446744073709551615");
    expect(probe.mapToDriverValue("773")).toBe("773");
  });

    expect(predicate(open)).toBe("closed_at is null");
    const queue = index("cases", "cases_queue_idx");
    expect(queue?.unique).toBe(false);
    expect(indexColumns(queue)).toEqual(["lane", "oldest_open_at"]);
    expect(predicate(queue)).toBe("closed_at is null");
    expect(indexColumns(index("cases", "cases_target_idx"))).toEqual(["target_type", "target_id", "opened_at"]);
    expect(checks("cases")).toEqual(["cases_closed_answered", "cases_lane", "cases_seq_order"]);
    expect(column("cases", "id")?.hasDefault).toBe(true);
    // No foreign key on the target: it names two tables.
    expect(foreignKeys("cases")).toEqual({});
  });

  test("no check lets a row through on a null: a statement always has its digest, a salt its form, and the two comparisons with a nullable value are null-safe", () => {
    // A CHECK passes when its expression is null, so `digest = encode(...)` alone would accept a statement with no digest.
    for (const [table, name] of [
      ["intake_items", "intake_items_statement"],
      ["appeals", "appeals_statement"],
    ] as const) {
      expect(checkSql(table, name), name).toContain(`"${table}"."statement_digest" is not null and "${table}"."statement_digest" = encode(sha256(`);
      expect(checkSql(table, name), name).toContain(`"${table}"."statement_salt" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'`);
    }
    expect(checkSql("staff_texts", "staff_texts_digest")).toContain(`"staff_texts"."salt" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' and "staff_texts"."digest" = encode(sha256(`);
    expect(checkSql("intake_items", "intake_items_case")).toBe(
      `("intake_items"."case_id" is null) = ("intake_items"."seq" is null) and ("intake_items"."case_id" is not null or "intake_items"."outcome" is not distinct from 'not_available')`,
    );
    expect(checkSql("decisions", "decisions_keyword")).toBe(`"decisions"."category_keyword" is null or "decisions"."ground" is not distinct from 'illegal'`);
  });

  test("the columns of decisions that the database forces: their types, and which carry a default", () => {
    // [name, SQL type, not null, default]; undefined where the column has none and the trigger of 0016 alone fills it.
    const forced = [
      ["appeal_id", "uuid", false, undefined],
      ["answers_from_seq", "integer", false, undefined],
      ["source", "decision_source", true, undefined],
      ["automated_detection", "boolean", true, false],
      ["automated_decision", "text", true, "not_automated"],
      ["territorial_scope", "text", true, "worldwide"],
      ["decided_at", "timestamp with time zone", true, undefined],
      ["xact", "xid8", true, undefined],
      ["puid", "text", true, undefined],
      // 3f: null while its author is not told (an order's held notice), which decisions_informed allows only with no mail.
      ["informed_at", "timestamp with time zone", false, undefined],
      ["suspect", "boolean", true, undefined],
      ["unseen", "boolean", true, false],
      ["needs_admin", "boolean", true, undefined],
      ["ended_interim", "boolean", true, undefined],
      ["author_mail", "delivery_state", true, "none"],
      ["author_mail_at", "timestamp with time zone", false, undefined],
    ] as const;
    for (const [name, type, notNull, fallback] of forced) {
      const c = column("decisions", name);
      expect(c?.getSQLType(), name).toBe(type);
      expect(c?.notNull, name).toBe(notNull);
      expect(c?.default, name).toBe(fallback);
    }
    // The Transparency Database's platform id: one per decision, never the internal id.
    expect(uniques("decisions")).toEqual([["decisions_puid_unique", ["puid"]]]);
  });

  test("the ledger: a measure once a decision, lifted at most once, and the columns the database forces", () => {
    expect(shape("decision_actions")).toEqual([
      ["id", "uuid", true],
      ["decision_id", "uuid", true],
      ["kind", "action_kind", true],
      ["media_id", "uuid", false],
      ["subject_account_id", "uuid", true],
      ["post_id", "uuid", false],
      ["reverses_action_id", "uuid", false],
      ["no_effect", "text", false],
      ["created_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      // 3e (design, section 6.1): three the key signs, four the trigger forces.
      ["days", "smallint", false],
      ["announced", "boolean", false],
      ["basis", "text", false],
      ["rests_on", "uuid[]", false],
      ["starts_at", "timestamp with time zone", false],
      ["ends_at", "timestamp with time zone", false],
      ["replaced", "boolean", false],
      // 3f (design, section 6.2): one the trigger forces from the order, one the key signs on a reinstatement.
      ["withhold_author", "boolean", false],
      ["order_ground", "text", false],
    ]);
    // None of the forced columns has a default: the triggers of 0016 and 0021 alone fill them.
    for (const name of ["subject_account_id", "post_id", "reverses_action_id", "no_effect", "created_at", "days", "announced", "basis", "rests_on", "starts_at", "ends_at", "replaced", "withhold_author", "order_ground"]) {
      expect(column("decision_actions", name)?.hasDefault, name).toBe(false);
    }
    const once = byName.get("decision_actions")!.uniqueConstraints.map((u) => [u.getName(), u.columns.map((c) => c.name), u.nullsNotDistinct]);
    expect(once).toEqual([["decision_actions_once", ["decision_id", "kind", "media_id"], true]]);
    const reversed = index("decision_actions", "decision_actions_reversed_once");
    expect(reversed?.unique).toBe(true);
    expect(indexColumns(reversed)).toEqual(["reverses_action_id"]);
    expect(predicate(reversed)).toBe("reverses_action_id is not null");
    expect(checks("decision_actions")).toEqual(["decision_actions_announced", "decision_actions_basis", "decision_actions_days", "decision_actions_no_effect", "decision_actions_order_ground"]);
    expect(checkSql("decision_actions", "decision_actions_order_ground")).toBe(`"decision_actions"."order_ground" in ('withdrawn', 'annulled', 'scrutiny', 'not_authentic', 'wrong_item')`);
    // Each check names columns only: no value of action_kind, which a check may not name in the migration that adds it.
    expect(checkSql("decision_actions", "decision_actions_days")).toBe(`"decision_actions"."days" between 1 and 30`);
    expect(checkSql("decision_actions", "decision_actions_basis")).toBe(
      `"decision_actions"."basis" in ('strikes', 'threat', 'terrorist', 'flood', 'protective', 'threat_repeat', 'ladder_end', 'reports')`,
    );
    expect(checkSql("decision_actions", "decision_actions_announced")).toBe(`"decision_actions"."announced" is null or "decision_actions"."basis" is not null`);
    expect(foreignKeys("decision_actions")).toEqual({
      decision_id: { table: "decisions", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "restrict" },
      reverses_action_id: { table: "decision_actions", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "no action" },
    });
    // 3c's seven measures and five reversals, then 3e's six measures and four reversals, in the order the migration adds them.
    expect(schema.actionKind.enumValues).toEqual([
      "withhold",
      "remove",
      "seal_media",
      "withhold_media",
      "remove_media",
      "reset_display_name",
      "reset_bio",
      "restore",
      "unseal_media",
      "restore_media",
      "restore_display_name",
      "restore_bio",
      "strike",
      "suspend",
      "terminate",
      "retire_handle",
      "warn_reporting",
      "restrict_reporting",
      "overrule",
      "lift_suspension",
      "unretire_handle",
      "lift_reporting",
      // 3f: the measure of an order decision and its reversal.
      "disable_by_order",
      "reinstate_by_order",
    ]);
  });
```
