  // The staff console's mails (3a design, section 7): to the staff account's own address, and never with a link.
  | "staff_key_added"
  | "staff_session_started"
  | "staff_key_suspect"
  | "staff_keys_revoked"
  // Moderation (3c design, section 7.15). To the people concerned: the receipt of a report or a notice, the daily update
  // of decisions on a person's reports, and the statement of reasons to the author of what a decision restricts. To
  // every staff account: the urgent lane's alert, the cases that wait longer than their response time, a burst of
  // decisions by one staff account, a staff account that reached its daily case limit, every reveal of who sent a
  // report, and every decision that lifted the protection of images reported as child sexual abuse material.
  | "notice_received"
  | "notice_update"
  | "moderation_decision"
  | "moderation_urgent"
  | "moderation_waiting"
  | "moderation_burst"
  | "moderation_reads"
  | "moderation_reveal"
  | "moderation_csam_lifted"
  // Account sanctions (3e design, sections 7.15 and 18, W.6): a decision's statement under a subject and a lead of its
  // own, for a suspension or termination announced or taken at once, for the answer to the person's reply, and for the
  // lift, the withdrawal or the end of one. And the auth module's own flat template, which no decision sends: the last
  // mail of a terminated account, after its take-down. And (Task 5) the statement of a warning about the account's
  // reports and of a restriction of them.
  | "suspension_announced"
  | "suspension_started_at_once"
  | "reply_answered"
  | "suspension_lifted"
  | "termination_final"
  | "reporting_warned"
  | "reporting_restricted"
  // Authorities' orders and the alert channel (3f design, sections 7.19 and 18, W.4): the staff alerts whose mail is their
  // push's sentence, each a kind of alert_outbox's: mail at the contact point, nobody answering it, its deadline
  // approaching, a mailbox korbat cannot read, and the phone alerts being down. Counts and UTC times only.
  | "contact_mail"
  | "contact_mail_escalated"
  | "order_due"
  | "mailbox_unreachable"
  | "alert_channel_down"
  // Task 2: an order opened, an order's record corrected, and the daily count of what orders given effect still miss.
  | "order_opened"
  | "order_corrected"
  | "order_unverified";

/** Every template but the one whose data is a structure: its data are flat strings. */
export type FlatTemplateName = Exclude<TemplateName, "notice_update">;

/**
 * One line of the daily update: the outcome of one item of a report (3c design, section 5). The moderation module sets
 * every field, from what korbat generated; none holds a report's words. The template chooses each of its sentences from
 * these fields alone.
 */
export interface NoticeUpdateLine {
  /** The notice's public reference. */
  ref: string;
  /** The item's position in its notice. */
  item: number;
  /** The item's korbat address, an account's under the handle as the notice named it. */
  link: string;
  /** The outcome's words, as the contracts' outcomeWords composes them, ending in a full stop. */
  outcome: string;
  /** The line answers a re-examination. */
  reexamination: boolean;
  /** The line gives the new outcome of an item that a review or a correction changed. */
  changed: boolean;
  /** A moderator's decision to take no action that can still be re-examined. */
  reexaminable: boolean;
  /** The line reads UNSEEN_NO_ACTION: such an answer is never final within korbat. */
  unseen: boolean;
  /** A link that named nothing, answered without a moderator. */
  automatic: boolean;
}

/**
 * The daily update's data. The moderation module gives the lines; the auth module adds whether the reader is signed in,
 * the receipts the 24-hour cap folded with their page links, the page link of each other notice the update has a line
 * for, and the terms' address. A signed-in update carries neither receipts nor pages.
 */
export interface NoticeUpdateData {
  signedIn: boolean;
  lines: NoticeUpdateLine[];
  receipts: { ref: string; time: string; items: string; pageUrl: string }[];
  pages: { ref: string; pageUrl: string }[];
  termsUrl?: string;
}

/** The daily update, whose data is a structure. */
export interface NoticeUpdateMessage {
  to: string;
  template: "notice_update";
  data: NoticeUpdateData;
}

/** A message of any other template: flat strings. */
export interface FlatMailMessage {
  to: string;
  template: FlatTemplateName;
  data: Record<string, string>;
}

/** A message is one of two shapes, told apart by its template. */
export type MailMessage = NoticeUpdateMessage | FlatMailMessage;

export interface Mailer {
  /**
   * Throws MailUnavailable when the message could not be handed to the relay, and its subclass MailRefused when the
   * relay answered that the recipient's address itself is bad, which no later try changes.
   */
  send(message: MailMessage): Promise<void>;
}

export class MailUnavailable extends Error {}

/**
 * The relay refused the recipient for good: no such mailbox or destination, a malformed address, a mailbox that moved or
 * a domain that takes no mail. A subclass of MailUnavailable, so a caller that does not tell the two apart behaves as
 * before; one that does records the mail as failed instead of trying again (3c design, section 5).
 */
export class MailRefused extends MailUnavailable {}

import { ACCOUNT_DELETION_WORDS, REPLY_AIM_HOURS, isTimeFact, renderAlert, type AlertKind } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { FlatTemplateName, MailMessage, NoticeUpdateData } from "./mailer";

export interface RenderedMail {
  subject: string;
  text: string;
  html: string;
}

const ESCAPES: Record<string, string> = { "&": "&amp;", "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;", '"': "&quot;", "'": "&#39;" };

function escapeHtml(value: string): string {
  return value.replace(/[&<>"']/g, (ch) => ESCAPES[ch]!);
}

function need(data: Record<string, string>, key: string): string {
  const value = data[key];
  if (value === undefined || value === "") throw new Error(`mail template data is missing "${key}"`);
  return value;
}

/** Plain paragraphs only: no images, no tracking, no anchor tags. URLs appear as text. */
function build(subject: string, paragraphs: string[]): RenderedMail {
  return {
    subject,
    text: `${paragraphs.join("\n\n")}\n`,
    html: `<!doctype html><html><body style="font-family:system-ui,sans-serif;line-height:1.5">${paragraphs
      .map((p) => `<p>${escapeHtml(p)}</p>`)
      .join("")}</body></html>`,
  };
}

/**
 * The subject of the statement's mail, by the decision's kind and outcome (3c design, section 7.15). The moderation
 * module names one of these keys; the words are written here only, so no caller passes a subject of its own.
 */
export const DECISION_MAIL_SUBJECTS = {
  seal_deciding: "korbat sealed images of yours while it decides",
  seal_final: "korbat sealed images of yours",
  post_deciding: "A post of yours is under review on korbat",
  profile_deciding: "korbat reset part of your profile while it decides",
  post_restricted: "korbat restricted a post of yours",
  profile_restricted: "korbat restricted part of your profile",
  lifted_deciding: "korbat lifted a restriction it placed while deciding",
  reversed: "korbat reversed a decision about your account",
  appeal_kept: "korbat answered your appeal",
} as const;

const STATEMENT_CLOSING = "Read it in korbat under Settings, Cases. korbat's emails never contain a link to act on a decision.";

function statementLines(data: Record<string, string>): string[] {

    .split(String.fromCharCode(10))
    .filter((paragraph) => paragraph.trim() !== "");
}

const LIFTED: Record<string, { subject: (what: string) => string; lead: (what: string) => string }> = {
  not_started: { subject: (what) => `korbat lifted the ${what} of your account`, lead: (what) => `korbat lifted the ${what} of your korbat account that it had announced: it never starts.` },
  running: { subject: (what) => `korbat lifted the ${what} of your account`, lead: (what) => `korbat lifted the ${what} of your korbat account. This ${what} no longer restricts your account.` },
  ended: { subject: (what) => `korbat lifted the ${what} of your account`, lead: (what) => `korbat lifted a past ${what} of your korbat account: it no longer counts toward a later suspension.` },
};

/** 3e (W.6): suspension_lifted's subject and lead when a reversal broke the measure's basis, by the period's state then. */
const LIFTED_BASIS: Record<string, { subject: (what: string) => string; lead: (what: string) => string }> = {
  not_started: {
    subject: (what) => `A ${what} of your account will not start`,
    lead: (what) => `korbat reversed a decision that the ${what} it announced for your korbat account rested on. The ${what} will not start.`,
  },
  running: {
    subject: (what) => `A ${what} of your account has ended`,
    lead: (what) => `The ${what} of your korbat account has ended, because a decision it rested on was reversed. This ${what} no longer restricts your account.`,
  },
  ended: {
    subject: (what) => `A past ${what} of your account no longer counts`,
    lead: (what) => `korbat reversed a decision that a past ${what} of your account rested on; that ${what} no longer counts.`,
  },
};

/** What a decision that lifted the protection of reported images did, as moderation_csam_lifted prints it. */
const CSAM_LIFTED_WHAT: Record<string, string> = {
  unsealed: "lifted a seal",
  dismissed: "answered a report or finding of child sexual abuse material without a seal",
};

/** The lanes as moderation_waiting names them, each with its response time. */
const WAITING_LANES = [
  { key: "lane0", name: "The urgent lane", time: "24 hours" },
  { key: "lane1", name: "Lane 1", time: "24 hours" },
  { key: "lane2", name: "Lane 2", time: "7 days" },
] as const;

/** The receipt's sentences, which notice_received and the receipts a notice_update carries share. */
const RECEIPT = {
  received: (ref: string, time: string, items: string) => `korbat received your report ${ref} at ${time}. It names: ${items}.`,
  page: (pageUrl: string) =>
    `To see where your report stands, ask for a re-examination of a decision, confirm that you sent it, or stop korbat's emails about reports to this address, open this page: ${pageUrl}`,
  terms: (termsUrl: string) => `How korbat handles reports, and what it keeps: ${termsUrl}.`,
};

export function renderTemplate(template: FlatTemplateName, data: Record<string, string>): RenderedMail {
  switch (template) {
    case "sign_in_code":
      return build("Your korbat sign-in code", [
        `Your sign-in code is ${need(data, "code")}.`,
        "It expires in 10 minutes. If you did not try to sign in, you can ignore this email; nobody can sign in without the code.",
      ]);
    case "sign_up_code":
      return build("Your korbat sign-up code", [
        `Your sign-up code is ${need(data, "code")}.`,
        "It expires in 10 minutes. If you did not try to create a korbat account, you can ignore this email.",
      ]);
    case "reauth_code":
      return build("Confirm it's you on korbat", [
        `Your confirmation code is ${need(data, "code")}.`,
        "It expires in 10 minutes. korbat asks for it before sensitive account changes.",
      ]);
    case "new_device":
      // The link runs the lockdown anchored at this sign-in (1c design, section 7.6): it reaches back a day, so a
      // passkey or two-factor set up just before, from the same stolen session, goes with it.
      return build("New sign-in to your korbat account", [
        `Your account was just signed in from a new device: ${need(data, "deviceLabel")}.`,
        "If this was you, there is nothing to do.",
        `If this was not you, open this link within 24 hours. It signs out every session, removes your password, and turns off every passkey and two-factor authentication set up since the day before this sign-in; then you sign in with a code sent to this address: ${need(data, "notMeUrl")}`,
      ]);
    case "account_locked":
      return build("Password sign-in paused on your korbat account", [
        `After several wrong passwords, password sign-in is paused for ${need(data, "minutes")} minutes.`,
        "You can still sign in with an emailed code. If you did not try to sign in, consider turning on two-factor authentication.",
      ]);
    case "mfa_enabled":
      return build("Two-factor authentication is on for your korbat account", [
        "Two-factor authentication was just turned on for your korbat account, and a new set of recovery codes was issued.",
        "If this was you, there is nothing to do. If not, sign in, open Security, and review your sessions and devices.",
      ]);
    case "mfa_disabled":
      return build("Two-factor authentication is off for your korbat account", [
        "Two-factor authentication was just turned off for your korbat account.",
        "If this was you, there is nothing to do. If not, sign in, open Security, turn it back on and sign out everywhere.",
      ]);
    case "password_changed":
      return build("Your korbat password changed", [
        "The password of your korbat account was just set or changed.",
        "If this was you, there is nothing to do. If not, sign in with an emailed code, open Security, set a new password and sign out everywhere.",
      ]);
    case "recovery_codes_regenerated":
      return build("New recovery codes for your korbat account", [
        "A new set of recovery codes was just issued for your korbat account. The old codes no longer work.",
        "If this was you, there is nothing to do. If not, sign in, open Security, and review your sessions and devices.",
      ]);
    case "sessions_revoked_all":
      return build("Signed out everywhere on korbat", [
        `Every session of your korbat account was just signed out (${need(data, "count")} in total).`,
        "If this was you, there is nothing to do. If not, sign in and set a new password.",
      ]);
    case "email_change_code":
      return build("Confirm your new korbat email address", [
        `Your confirmation code is ${need(data, "code")}.`,
        "It expires in 10 minutes. If you did not ask to move a korbat account to this address, you can ignore this email; nothing changes without the code.",
      ]);
    case "email_changed":
      // The undo link goes with the first change in a day only (flows/email-change.ts); a later change in that day
      // says where the link that works went, because signing in here is no longer possible.
      return build("Your korbat email address changed", [
        `The email address of your korbat account was just changed to ${need(data, "email")}. This address no longer belongs to the account.`,
        "Every session stays signed in. If this was you, there is nothing to do.",
        data.revertUrl
          ? `If this was not you, open this link within 24 hours. It moves the account back to this address, signs out every session, removes the password, and turns off every passkey and two-factor authentication set up since the day before the change; then you sign in with a code sent to this address: ${data.revertUrl}`
          : "If this was not you: the address had already changed less than a day ago, and the link sent then, to the address the account had before, can still move the account back there and sign out every session.",
      ]);
    case "email_change_reverted":
      return build("Your korbat account is back at this address", [
        "Your korbat account is back at this address, moved back from the link sent when its address changed, and every session was signed out.",
        "Sign in with a code sent to this address. The password was removed, and every passkey and two-factor authentication set up since the day before the change was turned off; set them up again from Security.",
      ]);
    case "badge_verified":
      return build("Your korbat account is verified", [
        "Your phone number was just confirmed, and your korbat account now shows the verified badge.",
        "korbat keeps only a keyed hash of the number, never the number itself. If this was not you, sign in, open Account, and remove the badge.",
      ]);
    case "badge_removed":
      return build("The verified badge was removed from your korbat account", [
        "The verified badge was just removed from your korbat account, and the phone number behind it was forgotten.",
        "If this was you, there is nothing to do. If not, sign in, open Security, and review your sessions and devices.",
      ]);
    case "delete_account_code":
      return build("Confirm deleting your korbat account", [
        `Someone asked to delete your korbat account. The confirmation code is ${need(data, "code")}.`,
        "It expires in 10 minutes, and nothing happens without it.",
        ACCOUNT_DELETION_WORDS,
        "If this was not you, do not enter the code: sign in, open Security, and revoke your other sessions.",
      ]);
    case "account_deleted":
      return build("Your korbat account was deleted", [
        "Your korbat account was deleted as you asked, and your handle stays reserved so nobody can take it.",
        ACCOUNT_DELETION_WORDS,
        "This cannot be undone. Thank you for having been part of korbat; you are welcome back with a new account any time.",
      ]);
    case "passkey_added":
      // The link runs the lockdown anchored at the passkey's creation (1c design, section 7.6): it reaches back a day,
      // so a password or two-factor set up just before the passkey, from the same stolen session, goes with it.
      return build("A passkey was added to your korbat account", [
        `A passkey named "${need(data, "name")}" was added to your korbat account from ${need(data, "deviceLabel")} at ${need(data, "time")}.`,
        "If this was you, there is nothing to do.",
        `If this was not you, open this link within 7 days. It removes this passkey, signs out every session, removes your password, and turns off every passkey and two-factor authentication set up since the day before this one was added; then you sign in with a code sent to this address: ${need(data, "removeUrl")}`,
      ]);
    case "passkey_removed":
      return build("A passkey was removed from your korbat account", [
        `The passkey named "${need(data, "name")}" was removed from your korbat account at ${need(data, "time")}. It can no longer sign in.`,
        "If this was you, there is nothing to do. If not, sign in, open Security, and review your passkeys, sessions and devices.",
      ]);
    case "passkey_suspect":
      // A counter that went backwards (1c design, section 2): the signature was right, so someone holds the key, and
      // either the authenticator was cloned or a backup was restored. Only the owner can tell, so the key stays off.
      return build("A passkey on your korbat account was switched off", [
        `A sign-in just used what looks like a copy of your passkey named "${need(data, "name")}", so korbat switched that passkey off. It can no longer sign in.`,
        "Sign in with a code sent to this address, open Security, remove it and add a new one. If you did not try to sign in just now, also review your sessions and devices.",
      ]);
    case "recovery_code_used":
      // A code spent at re-authentication (1c design, section 7.2): each of the ten works once, so the owner should know the count is down.
      return build("A recovery code was used on your korbat account", [
        "A recovery code was just used to confirm it's you on your korbat account. Each code works once; set up two-factor authentication again from Security to get a new set.",
        "If this was not you, sign in, open Security, sign out everywhere and set up two-factor authentication again.",
      ]);
    case "staff_key_added":
      return staffMail("A staff key was added to your korbat staff account", [
        `A staff key named "${need(data, "name")}" was registered for your korbat staff account at ${need(data, "time")}. It can open the staff console.`,
        "If this was you, there is nothing to do. If not, tell the operator at once; they revoke the key with the staff command line.",
      ]);
    case "staff_session_started":
      return staffMail("A staff session started on the korbat console", [
        `A staff session was started on the korbat console at ${need(data, "time")} with your staff key "${need(data, "name")}", from ${need(data, "browser")}.`,
        "If this was you, there is nothing to do. If not, someone holds that key: tell the operator at once; they revoke it and every session it opened with the staff command line.",
      ]);
    case "staff_key_suspect":
      // A counter that went backwards on a staff key (3a design, section 7): never passkey_suspect, whose remedy is the
      // app's Security screen; only the operator can enrol a replacement.
      return staffMail("A staff key on your korbat staff account was switched off", [
        `A use of your staff key "${need(data, "name")}" on the korbat console (a sign-in or a confirmation) looked like a copy of it, so korbat switched that key off and ended every staff session it opened. It can no longer open the console.`,
        "Ask the operator for a link to register a new key. If you did not use it just now, tell them so: someone else holds a copy of the key.",
      ]);
    case "staff_keys_revoked":
      // `names` is the list of the revoked keys' names, each in quotes, as the sender joins them.
      return staffMail("Staff keys revoked on your korbat staff account", [
        `These staff keys of your korbat staff account were revoked at ${need(data, "time")}: ${need(data, "names")}. They can no longer open the console, and every staff session they opened has ended.`,
        "If you expected this, there is nothing to do. If not, ask the operator why.",
      ]);
    case "notice_received":
      // The receipt of a report or a notice (3c design, section 7.15). `items` is the list of korbat links the report
      // named, as the sender joins them: built from parsed ids, an account's from the handle as it was named. With
      // `pageUrl` it goes to a signed-out notifier's address, and the link's fragment holds that contact's mail token,
      // which no server log sees; without it, to an account, whose reports are in the app.
      return userMail(`korbat received your report ${need(data, "ref")}`, [
        RECEIPT.received(need(data, "ref"), need(data, "time"), need(data, "items")),
        "A moderator decides each item that names something on korbat; a link that names nothing is answered automatically. You get one email with every decision, at most once a day.",
        data.pageUrl ? RECEIPT.page(data.pageUrl) : "You can follow it in korbat under Settings, Cases, Your reports.",
        RECEIPT.terms(need(data, "termsUrl")),
      ]);
    case "moderation_decision": {
      // The statement of reasons, to the author of what a decision restricts or lifts (3c design, section 7.15). The
      // subject is a key of the table above, and `statement` holds the statement's paragraphs, one per line, exactly as
      // statementParagraphs rendered them: the author's screen and the console's preview show the same words.
      const key = need(data, "subject");
      if (!Object.hasOwn(DECISION_MAIL_SUBJECTS, key)) throw new Error(`mail template data holds a subject that the statement's mail does not have: "${key}"`);
      const lines = need(data, "statement")
        .split("\n")
        .filter((paragraph) => paragraph.trim() !== "");
      return userMail(DECISION_MAIL_SUBJECTS[key as DecisionMailSubject], [...lines, STATEMENT_CLOSING]);
    }
    case "suspension_announced": {
      // 3e (design, W.6): a suspension or a termination announced with the reply window. Nothing is restricted yet; the
      // lead says when it starts and that a reply before then holds it, then the statement's paragraphs exactly as
      // rendered. Every time is the database's, printed as the notices print one; "sent" is all korbat knows of a mail.
      const terminated = need(data, "measure") === "terminate";
      const earliest = need(data, "earliestStart");
      const days = terminated ? "" : need(data, "days");
      const what = terminated ? "termination" : "suspension";
      const lead = `${terminated ? "korbat has decided to terminate your korbat account" : `korbat has decided to suspend your korbat account for ${days} ${days === "1" ? "day" : "days"}`}. Nothing is restricted yet. The ${what} starts ${need(data, "window")} hours after korbat sent this email, and not before ${earliest}.`;
      const reply = `You can reply before it starts: sign in to korbat, where this decision is always shown and a banner on every screen gives the exact time and a Reply button. A reply sent before ${earliest} is certainly in time, and holds the start until a moderator has answered you.`;
      return userMail(terminated ? "korbat has decided to terminate your account: you can reply first" : "korbat has decided to suspend your account: you can reply first", [
        lead,
        reply,
        "The decision and its reasons follow.",
        ...statementLines(data),
        STATEMENT_CLOSING,
      ]);
    }
    case "reply_answered": {
      // 3e (design, W.6): the answer to the person's reply, which kept the measure or reversed it; the answer's statement follows.
      const outcome = need(data, "outcome");
      if (outcome !== "kept" && outcome !== "reversed") throw new Error(`mail template data holds an outcome that reply_answered does not have: "${outcome}"`);
      const lead = outcome === "kept" ? "A moderator read your reply and kept the decision. The answer and its reasons follow." : "A moderator read your reply and reversed the decision. The answer follows.";
      return userMail("korbat answered your reply", [lead, ...statementLines(data), STATEMENT_CLOSING]);
    }
    case "termination_final": {
      // 3e (design, W.6): the auth module's own mail after the take-down of a terminated account, to the address read
      // before it. It names no reporter and no staff member, carries no link, and never says that korbat keeps nothing
      // when images of the account stay sealed for the authorities.
      const sealed = need(data, "imagesSealed") === "true";
      return userMail("korbat has closed your terminated account", [
        `korbat's decision of ${need(data, "decided")} to terminate your korbat account is final: the time to appeal has passed, or your appeal was answered and the decision kept, and no reply of yours is unanswered.`,
        "korbat has closed the account and is now deleting its posts and profile and every image it has not sealed, as that decision said. This cannot be undone. The handle stays reserved, so nobody else can take it.",
        [
          "korbat keeps nothing to recognise a new account of yours by.",
          ...(sealed ? ["Images of yours that korbat sealed stay with it for the authorities alone, as the decision that sealed them said."] : []),
          "A new account that carries on what this one was terminated for breaks korbat's terms.",
        ].join(" "),
      ]);
    }
    case "suspension_started_at_once": {
      // 3e (design, W.6): a suspension or a termination taken at once. The lead, then the statement's paragraphs exactly
      // as rendered, then what every statement mail ends with.
      const terminated = need(data, "measure") === "terminate";
      const days = terminated ? "" : need(data, "days");
      const lead = terminated
        ? "korbat terminated your korbat account. It did so at once, without notice beforehand; the reasons follow. You can reply and appeal in korbat from now: sign in and use the banner on any screen."
        : `korbat suspended your korbat account for ${days} ${days === "1" ? "day" : "days"}, until ${need(data, "endsAt")}. It did so at once, without notice beforehand; the reasons follow. You can reply and appeal in korbat from now: sign in and use the banner on any screen.`;
      return userMail(terminated ? "korbat terminated your account" : "korbat suspended your account", [lead, ...statementLines(data), STATEMENT_CLOSING]);
    }
    case "suspension_lifted": {
      // 3e (design, W.6): a lift of a suspension or a termination, or its end because a decision it rested on was
      // reversed, by where its period stood at that decision's time. No lead says "you can use your account as before":
      // another measure may still stand, so each says only that this one no longer restricts the account.
      const what = need(data, "measure") === "terminate" ? "termination" : "suspension";
      const why = need(data, "why");
      if (why === "replaced") {
        // A withdrawal to make room for another measure: never worded as an answer to the person's reply.
        const lead = `korbat withdrew the ${what} of your korbat account that it announced on ${need(data, "decidedAt")}, because it is taking another measure on your account.${data.replied === "true" ? " This is not a decision on your reply." : ""}`;
        return userMail(`korbat withdrew the ${what} it announced`, [lead, "The decision about the other measure reaches you separately.", ...statementLines(data), STATEMENT_CLOSING]);
      }
      const period = need(data, "period");
      const words = why === "basis" ? LIFTED_BASIS[period] : why === "lifted" ? LIFTED[period] : undefined;
      if (words === undefined) throw new Error(`mail template data holds a why or a period that suspension_lifted does not have: "${why}", "${period}"`);
      return userMail(words.subject(what), [words.lead(what), ...statementLines(data), STATEMENT_CLOSING]);
    }
    case "reporting_warned":
      // 3e (design, W.6, Task 5): a warning about the account's reports. It restricts nothing; the statement's paragraphs,
      // exactly as rendered, name the reports concerned and what may follow. No mail names who reported the person.
      return userMail("korbat warns you about your reports", [
        "korbat has looked at the reports your account sent under its rules and warns you about them. Nothing is restricted. The reasons, the reports concerned and what may follow are below.",
        ...statementLines(data),
        STATEMENT_CLOSING,
      ]);
    case "reporting_restricted": {
      // 3e (design, W.6, Task 5): a restriction of the account's reports under the rules, from its decision to its end.
      // Notices of illegal content stay open, and the lead says so before the statement's paragraphs.
      const days = need(data, "days");
      return userMail("korbat restricted your reports under its rules", [
        `korbat takes no reports under its rules from your account for ${days} ${days === "1" ? "day" : "days"}, until ${need(data, "endsAt")}. You can still report illegal content. The reasons follow.`,
        ...statementLines(data),
        STATEMENT_CLOSING,
      ]);
    }
    case "moderation_urgent": {
      // The alert for the urgent lane (3c design, section 7.12): counts and times only, to every staff account. A single
      // case is its own oldest, so its sentence gives one time and is worded for one.
      const lane = "in the urgent lane (child sexual abuse or exploitation, direct threats, violence, public security or self-harm)";
      return staffMail("korbat: a case is waiting in the urgent lane", [
        need(data, "count") === "1" ? `1 case ${lane} is waiting, since ${need(data, "oldest")}.` : `${need(data, "count")} cases ${lane} are waiting; the oldest since ${need(data, "oldest")}.`,
        // 3f (W.4): the same alert went to the phone on call as a push.
        "Open the staff console. The same alert went to the phone on call.",
      ]);
    }
    case "moderation_waiting": {
      // The queue-age alert (3c design, section 7.12): per lane the cases past its response time and since when the
      // oldest waits, and the cases that have held a measure taken while deciding for more than a day. A lane's pair is
      // there only for a lane with such a case; a single case is its own oldest and is worded as one.
      const lines: string[] = [];
      for (const lane of WAITING_LANES) {
        const count = data[`${lane.key}Count`];
        if (count === undefined || count === "") continue;
        const oldest = need(data, `${lane.key}Oldest`);
        lines.push(count === "1" ? `${lane.name}: 1 case waiting longer than ${lane.time}, since ${oldest}.` : `${lane.name}: ${count} cases waiting longer than ${lane.time}; the oldest since ${oldest}.`);
      }
      const held = data.interimCount;
      if (held !== undefined && held !== "") {
        lines.push(
          held === "1"
            ? "1 case has held a measure taken while deciding for more than 24 hours; its author cannot appeal until the case is decided."
            : `${held} cases have held a measure taken while deciding for more than 24 hours; their authors cannot appeal until the case is decided.`,
        );
      }
      // 3e (W.6): the replies to a suspension or a termination unanswered for longer than korbat's aim.
      const replies = data.replyCount;
      if (replies !== undefined && replies !== "") {
        const oldest = need(data, "replyOldest");
        lines.push(
          `${replies === "1" ? "1 reply to a suspension or termination has" : `${replies} replies to a suspension or termination have`} waited more than ${REPLY_AIM_HOURS} hours, ${replies === "1" ? "since" : "the oldest since"} ${oldest}. A reply sent before the start holds its suspension until someone answers.`,
        );
      }
      if (lines.length === 0) throw new Error("mail template data for moderation_waiting names nothing that waits");
      // 3f (W.4): the same reminder went to every staff phone as a push.
      return staffMail("korbat: cases are waiting longer than their response time", [...lines, "Open the staff console. The same reminder went to every staff phone."]);
    }
    case "moderation_burst": {
      // One staff account confirmed many decisions in a short time (3c design, section 7.5, step 4): every staff
      // account is told, since a stolen key decides at the speed of key prompts.
      const who = `@${need(data, "handle")}`;
      return staffMail("korbat: many staff decisions in a short time", [
        `The staff account ${who} confirmed ${need(data, "count")} decisions in the last 15 minutes.`,
        `Every staff account gets this email. If ${who} is your account and you did not confirm them, someone else holds your key: tell the operator at once.`,
        "If that was not expected, ask them; if their key may be in someone else's hands, the operator revokes it with staff.js revoke.",
      ]);
    }
    case "moderation_csam_lifted": {
      // A decision lifted a seal, or an admin answered a report or finding of child sexual abuse material without one
      // (3c design, section 7.5, step 4): neither can be undone once the images are served again, so every staff
      // account is told at once. It names the staff account and the time, never the case or its author.
      const who = `@${need(data, "handle")}`;
      const what = CSAM_LIFTED_WHAT[need(data, "what")];
      if (what === undefined) throw new Error(`mail template data holds a "what" that moderation_csam_lifted does not have: "${data.what}"`);
      return staffMail("korbat: reported images are no longer protected", [
        `The staff account ${who} confirmed a decision at ${need(data, "time")} that ${what}.`,
        "Unless another seal or another open report of this kind still covers them, the images its case reaches are served again as before and staff may open them. After an answer without a seal, whoever is on duty opens them the same day and, where one breaks a rule or the law, opens a finding on its post. Nobody at korbat could open those images while they were protected.",
        `Every staff account gets this email. If ${who} is your account and you did not confirm it, someone else holds your key: tell the operator at once.`,
        "The staff console's home screen lists every such decision of the last 30 days with its case. A seal for good is lifted only on the answer of the authority korbat reported the images to, and a seal taken while deciding only when it was taken in error: the operator compares this decision with their R2 records. If it was not expected, ask them; if their key may be in someone else's hands, the operator revokes it with staff.js revoke, and whoever is on duty opens a finding citing R2 on the post or the account and seals its images while deciding.",
      ]);
    }
    case "contact_mail":
    case "contact_mail_escalated":
    case "order_due":
    case "mailbox_unreachable":
    case "alert_channel_down":
    case "order_opened":
    case "order_corrected":
    case "order_unverified":
      return alertMail(template, data);
    case "moderation_reads": {
      // A staff account opened as many different cases today as one account may (3c design, section 7.3): every staff
      // account is told, the account itself included, since a stolen key reads at the speed of requests.
      const who = `@${need(data, "handle")}`;
      return staffMail("korbat: a staff account reached its daily case limit", [
        `The staff account ${who} opened ${need(data, "limit")} different cases today and cannot open others until midnight UTC.`,
        `Every staff account gets this email. If ${who} is your account and you did not open them, someone else holds your key: tell the operator at once.`,
        "If that was not expected, ask them. The operator raises the limit with staff.js limits.",
      ]);
    }
    case "moderation_reveal": {
      // Every reveal of who sent a report or a notice (3c design, section 7.3), to every staff account: a reveal cannot
      // be undone. It names the staff account, the time and the day's count, never the case or the person revealed.
      const who = `@${need(data, "handle")}`;
      return staffMail("korbat: a staff account revealed who sent a report", [
        `The staff account ${who} revealed who sent a report or notice at ${need(data, "time")}. That is ${need(data, "count")} of the ${need(data, "limit")} reveals one staff account may make today (UTC).`,
        `Every staff account gets this email. If ${who} is your account and you did not reveal it, someone else holds your key: tell the operator at once.`,
        "The staff console's home screen lists every reveal of the last 30 days with its case. If this one was not expected, ask them; if their key may be in someone else's hands, the operator revokes it with staff.js revoke.",
      ]);
    }
  }
}

const OUTSIDE_KORBAT = "go to court, or complain to the Digital Services Coordinator of the EU country where you live (Article 53 of the Digital Services Act).";

/**
 * The daily update of decisions on a person's reports (3c design, section 7.15), the one template whose data is a
 * structure. In this order: each receipt the 24-hour cap folded, with its page link, and after them once where korbat
 * says how it handles reports; one paragraph for each line; for a signed-out reader the page of each notice the update
 * has a line for; and, only when it carries a line, that nothing was automated, how to ask for a re-examination, what is
 * final within korbat, what to do about a wrong link, and the courts and the Digital Services Coordinator. Every
 * sentence is chosen from the lines' fields alone, and a line's outcome is printed as the moderation module composed it.
 */
export function renderNoticeUpdate(data: NoticeUpdateData): RenderedMail {
  const { lines, receipts, pages } = data;
  if (lines.length === 0 && receipts.length === 0) throw new Error("mail template data for notice_update holds nothing to tell: no line and no receipt");
  // An account's reports are followed in the app: its update never carries a link with a token.
  if (data.signedIn && (receipts.length > 0 || pages.length > 0)) throw new Error("mail template data for a signed-in notice_update holds a receipt or a page link");
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const receipt of receipts) out.push(RECEIPT.received(receipt.ref, receipt.time, receipt.items), RECEIPT.page(receipt.pageUrl));
  if (receipts.length > 0) {
    if (!data.termsUrl) throw new Error('mail template data is missing "termsUrl"');
    out.push(RECEIPT.terms(data.termsUrl));
  }
  for (const line of lines) {
    // The outcome's words end in their own full stop.
    const outcome = line.outcome.endsWith(".") ? line.outcome : `${line.outcome}.`;
    out.push(`${line.ref}, item ${line.item} (${line.link})${line.reexamination ? ", re-examined" : ""}: ${outcome}`);
  }
  for (const page of pages) out.push(`To see report ${page.ref} or ask for a re-examination of a decision on it, open this page: ${page.pageUrl}`);
  if (lines.length > 0) {
    const automatic = lines.some((line) => line.automatic);
    out.push(`No automated means were used to decide${automatic ? ", except for links found to name nothing on korbat, which were checked automatically" : ""}.`);
    const reexaminable = lines.some((line) => line.reexaminable);
    if (reexaminable) {
      out.push(
        `You can ask korbat once, within six months and free of charge, to re-examine a moderator's decision to take no action: it is decided again as a new report. ${
          data.signedIn ? "Use korbat's Settings, Cases, Your reports." : "Use the page linked in this email for that report."
        }`,
      );
    }
    // An answer given while nobody could open the images leaves the re-examination unspent, so it is never called final.
    if (lines.some((line) => line.changed || (line.reexamination && !line.unseen))) out.push("A decision changed on review or by a correction, or given on re-examination, is final within korbat.");
    if (automatic) out.push("If a link was wrong, send a new report with the right link.");
    out.push(`You can ${reexaminable ? "also " : ""}${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`);
  }
  return userMail(lines.length > 0 ? "Decisions on your reports to korbat" : "korbat received your reports", out);
}

/** A message as it is sent: the structured template by its own renderer, every other by renderTemplate. */
export function renderMail(message: MailMessage): RenderedMail {
  return message.template === "notice_update" ? renderNoticeUpdate(message.data) : renderTemplate(message.template, message.data);
}

/**
 * A moderation mail to a user: plain paragraphs as every mail, closed by the sentence that korbat's staff ask for
 * nothing by mail, so a message that asks for a password or a code, or for an answer, is known for a fake (3c design,
 * section 7.15).
 */
function userMail(subject: string, paragraphs: string[]): RenderedMail {
  return build(subject, [...paragraphs, "korbat staff never ask for your password or a code, and korbat does not read replies to this email."]);
}

/**
 * 3f (design, sections 7.19 and 18, W.4): a staff alert whose mail is its push's sentence. The subject is "korbat: " and
 * the kind's title, the paragraphs its sentence and its line of what to do, each the contracts' ALERT_TEXTS filled from
 * the row's facts by renderAlert, which refuses a fact of another name and anything but a count or a UTC time, so the
 * mail names no person, no content, no authority and no link. The data's `now` is when the mail is sent: a time prints
 * with its day only when that is not today's.
 */
function alertMail(kind: AlertKind, data: Record<string, string>): RenderedMail {
  const { now, ...facts } = data;
  if (now === undefined || now === "" || Number.isNaN(Date.parse(now))) throw new Error('mail template data is missing "now"');
  const counted = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(facts).map(([name, value]) => [name, isTimeFact(name) ? value : Number(value)]));
  const text = renderAlert(kind, counted, new Date(now));
  if (text.todo === null) throw new Error(`mail template ${kind} has no line of what to do: its mail is not its sentence`);
  return staffMail(`korbat: ${text.title}`, [text.sentence, text.todo]);
}

/**
 * A staff mail: plain paragraphs as every mail, closed by the sentence that no staff mail carries a link, so a message
 * that does carry one is known for a fake (3a design, section 7).
 */
function staffMail(subject: string, paragraphs: string[]): RenderedMail {
  return build(subject, [...paragraphs, "korbat never puts a link in a staff email."]);
}

export function imagePost(q: Db | DbTx, mediaId: string): Promise<string | null> {

/**
 * 3f (design, section 7.5): how many image rows each of these posts holds, for an order's screen, which counts a post's

   * (3c design, section 7.10): the purge asks for the files of the rows it was answered, and of no other. Still inside
   * that transaction it notes that those files are owed a request, so the rows cannot be gone for good without a record

  purgeOwner(tx: DbTx, ownerId: string): Promise<string[]>;

   * was taken already); then one empty request file per id, so asking twice is asking once; then what was
   * owed for them is settled. The account purge asks only after its transaction has committed, for the rows
   * that transaction deleted: a request cannot be taken back, and rows that a failed commit put back may be
   * frozen by a report before the purge runs again. When it throws, the deletion stays owed, and the sweeper
   * asks again at its next pass.
   */
  requestDeletion(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<void>;
  /**
   * The account's ready images that it is still shown, on a post or not, each with the checked open of its large
   * variant: the store is written by the worker and not trusted, so a file is read only when it is a plain file of the
   * store's own device no larger than a variant may be, and only up to the size that check measured

/** The account module's interface over this module's dependencies, as createMedia hands it out; the integration tests build it the same way. */
export function mediaForAccount(deps: MediaDeps): MediaForAccount {

    async purgeOwner(tx, ownerId) {
      const ids = await deps.repo.purgeOwner(tx, ownerId);
      await deps.files.oweDeletion(ids);
      return ids;
    },
    async requestDeletion(ids) {
      for (const id of ids) await deps.files.discardUpload(id);
      await deps.files.requestDeletion(ids);
      await deps.files.settleOwed(ids);
    },
    exportImages: async (ownerId) =>
      (await deps.repo.readyImages(ownerId)).map((id) => ({
        id,
        // The row is read again, with the list's own condition, right before the file is opened.
        open: async () => ((await deps.repo.isExportable(ownerId, id)) ? deps.files.openImage(id, "large") : null),

  };
}

export interface CreateMediaOptions {
  /** The korbat_api pool. The module never sees the auth pool. */
  apiDb: Db;
  /** The uploads volume, which the API writes, and the store volume, which it only reads. */
  uploadsDir: string;
  storeDir: string;
  formats: readonly MediaFormat[];
  minFreeBytes: number;
  /** See MEDIA_RECONCILE; defaults to `on`. */
  reconcile?: "on" | "off" | "force";
  logger: Logger;
  /** The auth module's requireSession: an onboarded account with CSRF and Origin checked. */
  requireSession: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** The auth module's resolveSession. The file routes run it themselves, and only when they must. */
  resolveSession: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** Image requests have their own per-IP bucket in the store the other limits use. */
  rateLimitStore: RateLimitStore;
  /** Built from the social module's write limits, so every per-account limit lives in one table. */
  enforceUploadLimit: MediaDeps["enforceUploadLimit"];
  now?: () => Date;
}

export function createMedia(options: CreateMediaOptions) {
  const deps: MediaDeps = {
    repo: createMediaRepo(options.apiDb),
    files: createMediaFiles({ uploadsDir: options.uploadsDir, storeDir: options.storeDir, log: options.logger }),
    formats: options.formats,
    minFreeBytes: options.minFreeBytes,
    reconcileMode: options.reconcile ?? "on",
    enforceUploadLimit: options.enforceUploadLimit,
    log: options.logger,
    now: options.now ?? (() => new Date()),
  };
  const forPosts: MediaForPosts = {
    attach: (tx, input) => deps.repo.attach(tx, input),
    detachAll: (tx, postId) => deps.repo.detachAll(tx, postId),
    requestDeletion: (ids) => deps.files.requestDeletion(ids),
    forPosts: (postIds) => deps.repo.forPosts(postIds),
  };
  const forAccount = mediaForAccount(deps);
  const forCases = mediaForCases(deps);
  return {
    deps,
    /** The interface the social module uses to put images on posts and read them back. */
    forPosts,
    /** The interface the account module uses. */
    forAccount,
    /** The interface the moderation module uses: an intake's holds, what a case reaches, the staff's image, the disposal. */
    forCases,
    /** Creates the uploads volume's directories. Call once before serving. */
    prepare: () => deps.files.prepare(),
    routes: mediaRoutes(deps, options.requireSession),
    /** Mounted before the global rate limit and session resolution. */
    fileRoutes: mediaFileRoutes(deps, { resolveSession: options.resolveSession, rateLimitStore: options.rateLimitStore }),
    /** One pass of housekeeping at the given time. The server runs it on a timer; tests call it directly. */
    sweep: (now: Date, options: { reconcile: boolean }) => sweep(deps, now, options),
    /** Starts sweeping every thirty seconds under the shared job lock, and returns the function that stops it. */
    startSweeper: (lock: JobLock) => createSweeper(deps, lock).start(),
    /** An advisory health check: the worker's heartbeat is fresh and the volumes have room. */
    async healthCheck(): Promise<void> {
      const age = await deps.files.heartbeatAge(deps.now().getTime());
      if (age === null || age > HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS) throw new Error("the image worker's heartbeat is missing or stale");
      if ((await deps.files.freeBytes()) < deps.minFreeBytes) throw new Error("free space on the media volumes is under the floor");
    },
  };
}

export type Media = ReturnType<typeof createMedia>;

import { and, eq, gt, inArray, isNotNull, isNull, lt, ne, or, sql, type SQL } from "drizzle-orm";
import { mediaPath } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { postMedia, posts, profiles, type Db, type DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import type { ResultFile } from "@korbat/media-protocol";
import { WRITE_CLOCK, closingJudgment, liveNotSuspended } from "../lib/standing";
import { MediaError, type PostImage } from "./context";

/**
 * Every SQL statement on post_media lives in this module's repository, on the korbat_api pool, and so does every
 * statement on media_holds, a case's evidence holds on image rows (3c design, section 5).
 *
 * Two rules of the database shape what is written here (3c design, section 6.1). The trigger post_media_keep decides for
 * every delete whether a row goes: it skips a row a hold retains and every row of a frozen post, so no delete below
 * filters for either, and each answers only the ids of the rows that are really gone, which are the only files a caller
 * may ask the worker to delete. And every statement that locks or deletes several image rows takes them in id order, so
 * that no two transactions ever lock one post's images in opposite orders.
 */

export interface MediaRow {
  id: string;
  ownerId: string;
  status: "processing" | "ready" | "failed";
  error: string | null;
  postId: string | null;
  width: number | null;
  height: number | null;
  blurhash: string | null;
  createdAt: Date;
  /** The image's own moderation state, which only a migrator-owned function writes. A sealed image is shown to nobody. */
  moderationState: "visible" | "withheld" | "removed" | "sealed";
}

/** One hold request of an intake: a post whose images the case holds as evidence, or an account whose images are only locked. */
export type HoldPair = { caseId: string; postId: string } | { ownerId: string };

/** An image as a case's snapshot lists it. The alt text is null for an image whose content was erased. */
export interface HeldImage {
  id: string;
  alt: string | null;
  width: number;
  height: number;
}

/** What a case about a post or an account reaches: counts, a day and a time, never an id, an alt text or a file. */
export interface CaseReach {
  /** The posts the case reaches that have image rows. */
  posts: number;
  images: number;
  sealed: number;
  /** The images korbat's server would still give to some reader. */
  served: number;
  /** The creation day, in UTC, of the newest post with image rows. */
  newestPostOn: string | null;
  /** When the newest post with a served image was created. */
  newestServedAt: Date | null;
}

/** Ids as one uuid[] parameter. */
const uuidArray = (ids: readonly string[]): SQL => sql`${`{${ids.join(",")}}`}::uuid[]`;

/**
 * An image the data export hands its owner: ready, in a state its author still sees (a sealed image is exported to
 * nobody, and a state this reader has not been taught is left out), not erased, and either on no post or on a post that
 * is neither deleted nor erased. A row that a case or a freeze kept after its post was deleted is in no export. The
 * query it is used in joins posts by the image's post.
 */
const EXPORTABLE = and(
  eq(postMedia.status, "ready"),
  inArray(postMedia.moderationState, ["visible", "withheld", "removed"]),
  isNull(postMedia.erasedAt),
  or(isNull(postMedia.postId), and(ne(posts.state, "deleted_by_author"), isNull(posts.erasedAt))),
);

/**
 * A row the disposal may take (3c design, section 7.9): nothing retains it (no hold stands, and its post is not frozen),
 * and its post is deleted, its owner is purged, or its post's content or its own was erased. `m` is the image row, `p`
 * its post when it has one, `o` its owner's profile. The freeze is read here only to keep kept rows out of a batch: for
 * each row that is deleted, post_media_keep decides.
 *
 * The marks and the freeze are one condition, a CASE that reads the freeze only for a row that carries a mark. As two
 * conditions the planner made the freeze the filter of the scan of post_media, since it names that table alone, and
 * called it for every attached image row in the table before any mark was tested: several index probes a row, seconds
 * for a table of thousands, however few rows were disposable. A CASE is evaluated in the order it is written, and this
 * one names all three tables, so it runs where they are joined.
 */
const DISPOSABLE = sql`(m.hold_until is null or m.hold_until <= now())
  and case when (p.state = 'deleted_by_author' or o.deleted_at is not null or p.erased_at is not null or m.erased_at is not null)
           then (m.post_id is null or not public.post_frozen(m.post_id))
           else false end`;

const columns = {
  id: postMedia.id,
  ownerId: postMedia.ownerId,
  status: postMedia.status,
  error: postMedia.error,
  postId: postMedia.postId,
  width: postMedia.width,
  height: postMedia.height,
  blurhash: postMedia.blurhash,
  createdAt: postMedia.createdAt,
  moderationState: postMedia.moderationState,
};

export function createMediaRepo(db: Db) {
  return {
    /** When the account was onboarded, which decides its upload tier. */
    async accountCreatedAt(userId: string): Promise<Date | null> {
      const rows = await db.select({ createdAt: profiles.createdAt }).from(profiles).where(eq(profiles.id, userId)).limit(1);
      return rows[0]?.createdAt ?? null;
    },

    /** Uploads of this account that are not on a post yet and did not fail. */
    async pendingCount(ownerId: string): Promise<number> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ count: sql<number>`count(*)::int` })
        .from(postMedia)
        .where(and(eq(postMedia.ownerId, ownerId), isNull(postMedia.postId), inArray(postMedia.status, ["processing", "ready"])));
      return rows[0]?.count ?? 0;
    },

    /**
     * The upload's row, as one statement that locks its owner's profile row FOR KEY SHARE and inserts only when the one
     * predicate holds (3e design, section 7.2): read in the statement that locks the row, by the clock. No row inserted
     * answers account_suspended, and the caller discards the received file. The statement's lock may wait for a holder
     * that only locks the row, which leaves its judgment as it was before the wait, so the transaction ends with the
     * closing judgment of the owner (3e's review): a deleted or suspended owner then rolls the insert back, answered
     * account_suspended as the statement answers both.
     */
    async insertProcessing(input: { id: string; ownerId: string; now: Date }): Promise<void> {
      await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        const inserted = await tx.execute(sql`
          with ok as (select p.id from profiles p where p.id = ${input.ownerId}::uuid and ${liveNotSuspended("p", WRITE_CLOCK)} for key share of p)
          insert into post_media (id, owner_id, status, created_at)
          select ${input.id}::uuid, ok.id, 'processing', ${input.now.toISOString()}::timestamptz from ok
          returning id`);
        if (inserted.length === 0) throw new MediaError("account_suspended", 403);
        const judged = await closingJudgment(tx, input.ownerId);
        if (!judged || judged.deleted || judged.suspended) throw new MediaError("account_suspended", 403);
      });
    },

    /**
     * One image row, for its owner's status. Two rules of the readers hold here (3c design, section 7.10): a row that a
     * case or a freeze keeps after its post was deleted, and a row whose content, its own or its post's, was erased, is
     * answered as a row that does not exist, to its owner too, so nothing tells the author that the row was kept; and a
     * sealed image is handed over without its blurhash, which is made from the image.
     */
    async find(id: string): Promise<MediaRow | null> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ ...columns, erasedAt: postMedia.erasedAt, postState: posts.state, postErasedAt: posts.erasedAt })
        .from(postMedia)
        .leftJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(eq(postMedia.id, id))
        .limit(1);
      const found = rows[0];
      if (!found || found.postState === "deleted_by_author" || found.erasedAt !== null || found.postErasedAt !== null) return null;
      const { erasedAt: _erasedAt, postState: _postState, postErasedAt: _postErasedAt, ...row } = found;
      return row.moderationState === "sealed" ? { ...row, blurhash: null } : row;
    },

    /** Records the worker's verdict, once. A row that is no longer processing is left as it is. */
    async finalize(id: string, result: ResultFile): Promise<boolean> {
      const values = result.status === "ready" ? { status: "ready" as const, width: result.width, height: result.height, blurhash: result.blurhash } : { status: "failed" as const, error: result.reason };
      const rows = await db.update(postMedia).set(values).where(and(eq(postMedia.id, id), eq(postMedia.status, "processing"))).returning({ id: postMedia.id });
      return rows.length === 1;

    /** Removes an upload of this account that is not on a post. */
    async deleteUnattached(id: string, ownerId: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const rows = await db.delete(postMedia).where(and(eq(postMedia.id, id), eq(postMedia.ownerId, ownerId), isNull(postMedia.postId))).returning({ id: postMedia.id });
      return rows.length === 1;
    },

    /**
     * What serving an image file depends on: whether it is ready, its own moderation state, its post's state and author,
     * and whether its content or its post's was erased.
     */
    async fileAccess(id: string): Promise<{ status: MediaRow["status"]; mediaState: MediaRow["moderationState"]; postState: string | null; authorId: string | null; erased: boolean } | null> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ status: postMedia.status, mediaState: postMedia.moderationState, postState: posts.state, authorId: posts.authorId, erasedAt: postMedia.erasedAt, postErasedAt: posts.erasedAt })
        .from(postMedia)
        .leftJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(eq(postMedia.id, id))
        .limit(1);

      return { status: found.status, mediaState: found.mediaState, postState: found.postState, authorId: found.authorId, erased: found.erasedAt !== null || found.postErasedAt !== null };

    /**
     * Puts images on a post, inside the transaction that creates it. Each must belong to the author,
     * be ready and be on no post yet; anything else rolls the post back.
     */
    async attach(tx: DbTx, input: { postId: string; ownerId: string; items: readonly { id: string; alt: string }[] }): Promise<void> {
      for (const [position, item] of input.items.entries()) {
        const rows = await tx
          .update(postMedia)
          .set({ postId: input.postId, position, altText: item.alt })
          .where(and(eq(postMedia.id, item.id), eq(postMedia.ownerId, input.ownerId), isNull(postMedia.postId), eq(postMedia.status, "ready")))
          .returning({ id: postMedia.id });

      }
    },

    /**
     * Removes a post's images, inside the transaction that deletes it, and says which files to delete afterwards. The
     * rows are taken in id order, under row locks, with no filter of its own: the keep trigger skips every row a case
     * holds and every row of a frozen post, and RETURNING omits them, so no file of a kept row is asked for. A plain
     * delete by post takes the rows in its scan's order, and deadlocked with an intake that locks the same rows by id.
     */
    async detachAll(tx: DbTx, postId: string): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = (await tx.execute(
        sql`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where post_id = ${postId}::uuid order by id for update) returning id`,
      )) as unknown as { id: string }[];
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * Removes every image row of the owner, on a post or not, whatever its state, inside the transaction
     * that purges the account, and says which files to delete afterwards (1b design, section 7.6). In id order under
     * row locks and with no filter, as detachAll: the keep trigger decides which rows stay.
     */
    async purgeOwner(tx: DbTx, ownerId: string): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = (await tx.execute(
        sql`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where owner_id = ${ownerId}::uuid order by id for update) returning id`,
      )) as unknown as { id: string }[];
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * The images of a page of posts, in one query, in their order on each post, each with its own moderation state:
     * what the state means for a reader is the view builder's to say. A sealed image is its id and its state only:
     * nobody is given its size, its blurhash, its alt text or a path. An image of a deleted post, and one whose content
     * or whose post's was erased, is given to nobody, its owner included, so no view and no export names a row that a
     * case or a freeze kept. A state this reader has not been taught is left out.
     */
    async forPosts(postIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, PostImage[]>> {
      const byPost = new Map<string, PostImage[]>();
      if (postIds.length === 0) return byPost;
      const rows = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id, postId: postMedia.postId, width: postMedia.width, height: postMedia.height, blurhash: postMedia.blurhash, altText: postMedia.altText, state: postMedia.moderationState })
        .from(postMedia)
        .innerJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(and(inArray(postMedia.postId, [...postIds]), eq(postMedia.status, "ready"), ne(posts.state, "deleted_by_author"), isNull(postMedia.erasedAt), isNull(posts.erasedAt)))
        .orderBy(postMedia.postId, postMedia.position);
      for (const row of rows) {
        if (!row.postId) continue;
        let image: PostImage;
        if (row.state === "sealed") image = { id: row.id, state: "sealed" };
        else if (row.state === "visible" || row.state === "withheld" || row.state === "removed") {
          if (row.width === null || row.height === null || row.blurhash === null) continue;
          image = { id: row.id, state: row.state, width: row.width, height: row.height, blurhash: row.blurhash, alt: row.altText ?? "", small: mediaPath(row.id, "small"), large: mediaPath(row.id, "large") };
        } else {
          // A state added later does not compile until this reader says who is given it.
          const unknown: never = row.state;
          void unknown;
          continue;
        }
        byPost.set(row.postId, [...(byPost.get(row.postId) ?? []), image]);
      }
      return byPost;
    },

    /**
     * Every image of the account that the data export takes a file for, on a post or not, oldest first: the ready ones
     * the account still sees (EXPORTABLE). A withheld or removed image stays with its author; a sealed image, an image
     * of a deleted post and an erased one are exported to nobody.
     */
    async readyImages(ownerId: string): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id })
        .from(postMedia)
        .leftJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(and(eq(postMedia.ownerId, ownerId), EXPORTABLE))
        .orderBy(postMedia.createdAt, postMedia.id);
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * Whether readyImages would still list this image of the owner: the export reads the row again when it opens each
     * file, so an image that was sealed, erased or deleted with its post while the archive streams is left out of it.
     */
    async isExportable(ownerId: string, id: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id })
        .from(postMedia)
        .leftJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(and(eq(postMedia.id, id), eq(postMedia.ownerId, ownerId), EXPORTABLE))
        .limit(1);
      return rows.length === 1;
    },

    /** Uploads that still wait for the worker's verdict. */
    async processingIds(): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db.select({ id: postMedia.id }).from(postMedia).where(eq(postMedia.status, "processing")).orderBy(postMedia.createdAt);
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /** Fails uploads the worker has not answered since `before`, and says which. */
    async failStale(before: Date): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db
        .update(postMedia)
        .set({ status: "failed", error: "processing_failed" })
        .where(and(eq(postMedia.status, "processing"), lt(postMedia.createdAt, before)))
        .returning({ id: postMedia.id });
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /** Removes uploads made before `before` that were never put on a post, whatever their state, and says which. */
    async deleteUnattachedBefore(before: Date): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db.delete(postMedia).where(and(isNull(postMedia.postId), lt(postMedia.createdAt, before))).returning({ id: postMedia.id });
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * Which of these ids have a row, whatever the row's state: the reconcile pass asks it which stored files belong to
     * no row, so a row that a hold or a freeze keeps must be seen here, or its files would be swept as orphans.
     */
    async existing(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<Set<string>> {
      if (ids.length === 0) return new Set();
      const rows = await db.select({ id: postMedia.id }).from(postMedia).where(inArray(postMedia.id, [...ids]));
      return new Set(rows.map((row) => row.id));
    },

    /** Removes a row whatever its state. Used when an upload could not be handed to the worker. */
    async deleteRow(id: string): Promise<void> {
      await db.delete(postMedia).where(eq(postMedia.id, id));
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ what moderation cases need

    /**
     * An intake's holds (3c design, sections 5 and 7.1, step 4), inside the intake's transaction. First one statement
     * locks, FOR KEY SHARE and in one id order, every image row the pairs name: the rows of each post and, for an owner
     * pair, every row of that owner that is on a post (an attached row's owner is its post's author, so those are the
     * images of the account's posts). The posts are read there, never locked. The lock is what makes a delete that races
     * the intake wait and then read the intake's committed item; a row whose delete committed first is not returned.
     * Then, for the post pairs only, the case's hold goes on each returned row that has no unreleased hold from that case
     * and is not erased, in id order, which is the order the holds are released in: an owner pair gets no hold, since the
     * images of a frozen post are kept whether a hold stands or not. It answers, for each post pair, the post's images
     * in position order, an erased one without its alt text; an empty list means the images are gone.
     */
    async hold(tx: DbTx, pairs: readonly HoldPair[]): Promise<Map<string, HeldImage[]>> {
      const caseOf = new Map<string, string>();
      const owners: string[] = [];
      for (const pair of pairs) {
        if ("postId" in pair) caseOf.set(pair.postId, pair.caseId);
        else owners.push(pair.ownerId);
      }
      const held = new Map<string, HeldImage[]>([...caseOf.keys()].map((postId) => [postId, []]));
      if (caseOf.size === 0 && owners.length === 0) return held;

      const locked = (await tx.execute(sql`
        select m.id, m.post_id, m.position, m.width, m.height, m.alt_text, (m.erased_at is not null or p.erased_at is not null) as erased
        from post_media m join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
        where m.post_id = any(${uuidArray([...caseOf.keys()])}) or m.owner_id = any(${uuidArray(owners)})
        order by m.id for key share of m`)) as unknown as { id: string; post_id: string; position: number; width: number; height: number; alt_text: string | null; erased: boolean }[];

      // The rows came back in id order; the holds are placed in that order too.
      const toHold = locked.filter((row) => caseOf.has(row.post_id) && !row.erased);
      if (toHold.length > 0) {
        await tx.execute(sql`
          insert into media_holds (media_id, case_id)
          select v.media_id, v.case_id
          from unnest(${uuidArray(toHold.map((row) => row.id))}, ${uuidArray(toHold.map((row) => caseOf.get(row.post_id)!))}) as v(media_id, case_id)
          where not exists (select 1 from media_holds h where h.media_id = v.media_id and h.case_id = v.case_id and h.released_at is null)
          order by v.media_id`);
      }

      for (const row of [...locked].sort((a, b) => a.position - b.position)) {
        held.get(row.post_id)?.push({ id: row.id, alt: row.erased ? null : (row.alt_text ?? ""), width: row.width, height: row.height });
      }
      return held;
    },

    /**
     * What a case about this post or this account reaches (3c design, section 6.1): the post itself, or every post
     * whose author is the account, whatever its state. One statement that locks nothing.
     */
    async reach(target: { type: "post" | "account"; id: string }): Promise<CaseReach> {
      const served = sql`m.moderation_state <> 'sealed' and p.state <> 'deleted_by_author' and m.erased_at is null and p.erased_at is null`;
      const reached = target.type === "post" ? sql`m.post_id = ${target.id}::uuid` : sql`p.author_id = ${target.id}::uuid`;
      const [row] = (await db.execute(sql`
        select count(distinct m.post_id)::int as posts,
               count(*)::int as images,
               (count(*) filter (where m.moderation_state = 'sealed'))::int as sealed,
               (count(*) filter (where ${served}))::int as served,
               to_char(max(p.created_at) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD') as newest_post_on,
               to_char(max(p.created_at) filter (where ${served}) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as newest_served_at
        from post_media m join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
        where ${reached}`)) as unknown as { posts: number; images: number; sealed: number; served: number; newest_post_on: string | null; newest_served_at: string | null }[];
      return {
        posts: row!.posts,
        images: row!.images,
        sealed: row!.sealed,
        served: row!.served,
        newestPostOn: row!.newest_post_on,
        newestServedAt: row!.newest_served_at === null ? null : new Date(row!.newest_served_at),
      };
    },

    /**
     * What opening an image for staff depends on, in one query: the row with its post, its size and its own state,
     * whether its content or its post's was erased, and whether its post is frozen now. Null when no row has the id or
     * the image is on no post.
     */
    async staffAccess(id: string): Promise<{ postId: string; status: MediaRow["status"]; width: number | null; height: number | null; mediaState: MediaRow["moderationState"]; erased: boolean; frozen: boolean } | null> {
      const [row] = (await db.execute(sql`
        select m.post_id, m.status, m.width, m.height, m.moderation_state, (m.erased_at is not null or p.erased_at is not null) as erased, public.post_frozen(m.post_id) as frozen
        from post_media m join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
        where m.id = ${id}::uuid`)) as unknown as { post_id: string; status: MediaRow["status"]; width: number | null; height: number | null; moderation_state: MediaRow["moderationState"]; erased: boolean; frozen: boolean }[];
      if (!row) return null;
      return { postId: row.post_id, status: row.status, width: row.width, height: row.height, mediaState: row.moderation_state, erased: row.erased, frozen: row.frozen };
    },

    /**
     * A page of the image rows that are on a post, in id order after `afterId` (from the start when it is null): each
     * one's id, its post, its stored moderation state and when its content was erased. It locks nothing and gives nothing
     * of an image itself. The staff command line's text-verify reads every such row through it, a page at a time, to
     * hold the stored states to what the ledger of measures says they must be.
     */
    /**
     * 3f (design, section 7.4): the post an image's address belongs to, or null when no attached image row has the id. An
     * order that names a picture's address names its post; this is a read, and it holds no row.
     */
    async imagePost(q: Pick<Db, "select"> | Pick<DbTx, "select">, mediaId: string): Promise<string | null> {
      const [row] = await q.select({ postId: postMedia.postId }).from(postMedia).where(and(eq(postMedia.id, mediaId), isNotNull(postMedia.postId))).limit(1);
      return row?.postId ?? null;
    },

    /** 3f (design, section 7.5): how many image rows each of these posts holds, for an order's screen; a post with none is left out. */
    async imageCounts(q: Pick<Db, "select"> | Pick<DbTx, "select">, postIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, number>> {
      if (postIds.length === 0) return new Map();
      const found = await q
        .select({ postId: postMedia.postId, count: sql<number>`count(*)::int` })
        .from(postMedia)
        .where(inArray(postMedia.postId, [...postIds]))
        .groupBy(postMedia.postId);
      return new Map(found.map((row) => [row.postId!, row.count]));
    },

    async moderationStates(afterId: string | null, limit: number): Promise<{ id: string; postId: string; moderationState: MediaRow["moderationState"]; erasedAt: Date | null }[]> {
      const found = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id, postId: postMedia.postId, moderationState: postMedia.moderationState, erasedAt: postMedia.erasedAt })
        .from(postMedia)
        .where(and(isNotNull(postMedia.postId), afterId === null ? undefined : gt(postMedia.id, afterId)))
        .orderBy(postMedia.id)
        .limit(limit);
      return found.map((row) => ({ id: row.id, postId: row.postId!, moderationState: row.moderationState, erasedAt: row.erasedAt }));
    },

    /**
     * Deletes at most `limit` disposable rows (DISPOSABLE), the lowest ids first, inside the caller's transaction, and
     * answers the ids of the rows that are gone, in id order. The candidates are locked in id order inside the delete,
     * so the disposal and an intake's hold never lock one post's images in opposite orders; a candidate that another
     * transaction is making retained is waited for, checked again and skipped, and the batch is filled from the next ids.
     * The keep trigger decides for each row: a report that froze a candidate's post after this statement began is not
     * seen by its filter, and is seen by the trigger.
     *
     * The candidates are a materialized common table expression, which runs once. As a plain sub-select of the delete
     * they could run again for every row the delete looks at, when the planner joins the two by a nested loop: each run
     * skips the rows this statement has deleted already and lets the next ones in, so one call deleted more than its
     * limit (measured: 33 rows under a limit of 25).
     */
    async dropDisposable(tx: DbTx, limit: number): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = (await tx.execute(sql`
        with batch as materialized (
          select m.id
          from post_media m
          join profiles o on o.id = m.owner_id
          left join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
          where ${DISPOSABLE}
          order by m.id
          limit ${limit}
          for update of m)
        delete from post_media where id in (select id from batch)
        returning id`)) as unknown as { id: string }[];
      return rows.map((row) => row.id).sort();
    },

    /**
     * How many rows the disposal should have taken by now: every disposable row none of whose holds ended, and none of
     * whose marks (its own erasure, its post's deletion or erasure) was set, within the last day. A hold ends when it is
     * released or when its time passes, whichever comes first. A row whose freeze ended within the last day may be
     * counted until the next round takes it: nothing records when a freeze ends.
     */
    async overdueDeletions(): Promise<number> {
      const [row] = (await db.execute(sql`
        select count(*)::int as n
        from post_media m
        join profiles o on o.id = m.owner_id
        left join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
        where ${DISPOSABLE}
          and not exists (select 1 from media_holds h where h.media_id = m.id and least(h.released_at, h.until) > now() - interval '1 day')
          and (m.erased_at is null or m.erased_at <= now() - interval '1 day')
          and (p.deleted_at is null or p.deleted_at <= now() - interval '1 day')
          and (p.erased_at is null or p.erased_at <= now() - interval '1 day')`)) as unknown as { n: number }[];
      return row!.n;
    },
  };
}

export type MediaRepo = ReturnType<typeof createMediaRepo>;
